items.defectStatement: In the `.group-member-info .name` rule (line 522), the diff changed the original `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to a `dark-light-choose` whose light-theme argument uses 50% lightness. Every other converted line used 50% in the original, but this one used 30%, so the name text in the light theme is now lighter (medium grey) than before.
obligations: The light-theme (first) argument of the color on line 522 must be `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, restoring the original light-theme appearance.
The declaration must still use `dark-light-choose(...)` with a dark-theme argument based on `$secondary`, so dark-theme support is kept.
The other properties of the rule must be unchanged, and the `.title` rule (line 527) must be left at 50%.
items.notes: The suggested dark-theme value of `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)` is a reasonable mirror of 30% on the primary scale, but it is not mandatory. Keeping `$secondary` at 50% (or a similar value) should also be accepted. The essential fix is restoring 30% in the light-theme argument.

items.defectStatement: `totalPages` (lines 11-14) computes `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which is one too many when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 members, limit 50 gives 2). As a result `showingLast` is false on the real last page, and `next` can move offset to user_count, showing an empty page.
obligations: totalPages must equal the ceiling of user_count/limit: exact multiples give user_count/limit pages, and non-multiples still round up (e.g. 51/50 gives 2).
totalPages must still return 0 when user_count is 0, keeping consistency with currentPage and showingFirst/showingLast.
The computed property must keep depending on both `limit` and `user_count`.
items.notes: Only lines 11-14 are cited. The suggested change to the `next` action is outside the cited range and is not required: once totalPages is correct, the `showingLast` guard already stops `next` on the real last page. Any equivalent ceiling formula is acceptable, e.g. `Math.ceil(n/l)` or `Math.floor((n-1)/l)+1` for n>0.

items.defectStatement: BlockedEmail.should_block? (line 12) looks up the record with an exact `where(email: email)` match. Unless the column is case-insensitive or both sides are normalized, a blocked address can get past the check by changing the case of the submitted email (e.g. `Bad@Spammers.org` vs stored `bad@spammers.org`).
obligations: The lookup on line 12 must find the blocked record whatever the letter case of the submitted email or the stored email, e.g. by comparing lower(email) against the downcased input.
Exact-case matches must still find the record. The result must still be bound to `record` so the match_count/last_match_at update and the action_type check keep working.
A nil or non-string email must not raise, e.g. use `email.to_s.downcase` or equivalent.
items.notes: The fix is confined to line 12, so lowercasing stored emails or adding a callback is out of scope. A case-insensitive query alone (lower(email) = downcased input) fully fixes the cited line. Arel `matches` or ILIKE are acceptable only if wildcard characters (`%`, `_`) in the input are escaped. Downcasing only the input, without lowering the column, is insufficient unless stored values are already guaranteed lowercase, and nothing shown guarantees that. The claims about User.new_from_params are not visible in this file and are not required to verify the defect.

items.defectStatement: In `perform_retrieve` (lines 40-42), an embed request for a URL that has no TopicEmbed yet calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously. That job imports every item in the RSS feed, so a single page view triggers O(N) `TopicEmbed.import` DB work even though only one URL (`@embed_url`) is wanted.
obligations: The feed path must not run a full, unbounded import of every feed item synchronously for one embed request. Valid approaches: limit processing to the item matching `@embed_url`, stop once it is imported, or enqueue the poll asynchronously.
Keep the behaviour when `feed_polling_enabled?` is false: go straight to `fetch_http`.
After the feed attempt, return without calling `fetch_http` if a TopicEmbed for `@embed_url` exists. Otherwise fall back to `fetch_http`.
Any change to how the PollFeed job is invoked must stay compatible with its existing scheduled use (it is called with `{}`).
items.notes: The fix is restricted to lines 40-42, so the most practical options are: pass the target URL in the job args (e.g. `execute(embed_url: @embed_url)`), or enqueue the job (`Jobs.enqueue(:poll_feed)`) instead of running it inline. Either is acceptable. If the job is enqueued, the post-poll exists? check becomes ineffective for this request, and the code should fall through to `fetch_http`. That is acceptable as long as no duplicate import results. The PollFeed internals are not shown here, so a fix that passes args the job ignores is not a real fix unless it is plausibly paired with a job change. The finding's suggestion to break the loop early also requires changing the job, which is outside the cited lines. Do not accept a fix that just deletes feed polling without any fallback reasoning.

items.defectStatement: `record_for_host` (lines 10-18) looks up records by `uri.host` only, which drops the port. The validation regex (line 2) and the `before_validation` stripping both allow a stored host like `example.com:8080`, so such records can never be matched and embedding from those hosts is silently denied.
obligations: When the incoming URL has a non-default port (`uri.port != uri.default_port`), the lookup must match a stored `host:port` value such as `example.com:8080`.
URLs with no port or the default port must still match stored entries without a port, as they do today. For example, `http://example.com/path` must match a stored `example.com`.
Keep returning a falsy value for unparseable input or input without a host, so `host_allowed?` stays false.
The comparison must stay case-insensitive against `lower(host)`, so the value compared should be lowercased (or equivalent).
items.notes: Only lines 10-18 can be changed, so the finding's alternative of rejecting ports in the validation (line 2) is not achievable here and must not be required. Acceptable fixes include: matching on `host:port` only, or trying `host:port` and falling back to the bare host (existing records without a port still allow any port). Do not insist on one of these. Matching a stored explicit default port (e.g. `example.com:80`) is a nice-to-have, not required. The current code also compares an un-lowercased `uri.host` to `lower(host)`; fixing this is welcome but secondary.

items.defectStatement: In `website_name` (lines 144-146), the equal-label-count branch treats two hosts as sharing a parent domain whenever they match after dropping the first label. Hosts on a multi-label public suffix (e.g. `forum.co.uk` vs `evil.co.uk`, both reducing to `co.uk`) therefore count as same-site, and the website's full URL path is exposed for an unrelated domain.
obligations: When the website and forum hosts share only a public suffix (e.g. `evil.co.uk` vs `forum.co.uk`, `a.com.au` vs `b.com.au`), the branch must return only `website_host`, without the path.

Genuine sibling subdomains of the same registrable domain must still return `website_host + path`. Examples: `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`, and `www.example.co.uk` vs `forum.example.co.uk`.
Hosts with different parent domains must still return only `website_host`, with no exception raised. This includes hosts a suffix parser may reject, such as IPs or `localhost`.
items.notes: Valid fixes include comparing registrable domains via the public_suffix gem (if it is available or added) or another suffix-aware check. The finding's alternative of 'at least three labels after removing the subdomain' is wrong as stated: it would reject the intended `www.example.com`/`forum.example.com` case, which leaves only two labels, so do not accept it unless it preserves that case. Line 149 has a related flaw outside the cited range (website `co.uk` vs forum `forum.co.uk`). Fixing it is optional and should not be required.

items.defectStatement: In validateUploadedFile (line 182), the max upload size is hardcoded to 10*1024 KB instead of being read from Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']. The client-side check therefore ignores the configured max_image_size_kb and max_attachment_size_kb. It rejects files the server would accept when a limit is set above 10 MB, and lets through files larger than a configured lower limit.
obligations: maxSizeKB must come from the site setting matching the upload type: max_image_size_kb for type 'image' and max_attachment_size_kb for type 'attachment'. It must not be a constant.
Keep the comparison against fileSizeKB = file.size / 1024. When the file is too large, the function must still show bootbox.alert with I18n 'post.errors.file_too_large' and return false.
The max_size_kb value passed to the alert must be the same configured limit that was used for the check.
Files within the limit must still fall through so the function returns true.
items.notes: The diff also hardcodes 10 MB in the 413 handler (line 246). That line is outside the cited range, so do not require it to be fixed. Any equivalent lookup of the per-type setting is acceptable, e.g. bracket-notation concatenation or a ternary choosing between max_image_size_kb and max_attachment_size_kb. Reject a fix that only changes the constant or that always uses max_image_size_kb.

items.defectStatement: In the save success callback (line 38), the host's category is always set to Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')), which is the client-submitted value. When categoryId is null (a new host saved with no category chosen), findById returns undefined. The client then shows an empty category, even though the server assigned a default (uncategorized) category, until the page is reloaded.
obligations: After a successful save where categoryId is null, host.category must reflect the server's resulting category (e.g. the category_id from the save response, or the uncategorized category). It must not be cleared or left undefined.
When a non-null categoryId was selected, host.category must still be set to that category after save.
Saving must still set editToggled to false on success, and errors must still go to popupAjaxError.
The category update must happen only after the save promise resolves successfully.
items.notes: Several fixes are valid: read category_id from the save result or payload and resolve it with findById; fall back to the site's uncategorized category id when categoryId is null; or only override the category when categoryId is non-null and otherwise use the category the server returned. Whether the store's save result exposes the payload depends on the Discourse store API; a grader should accept any approach that yields the server-assigned category. Keeping the existing category unchanged on null is insufficient for new hosts, which have no category at all. Do not require changes outside lines 37-38.

items.defectStatement: In `website_name`'s fallback branch (line 149), only `discourse_host.ends_with?("." + website_host)` is checked, which matches only when the website is the parent domain of the instance. When the website host is a subdomain of the instance host (e.g. website `forum.example.com`, instance `example.com`), the check is false and the method returns the bare host, dropping the path.
obligations: When the website host is a dot-delimited subdomain of the instance host (e.g. `forum.example.com` vs `example.com`), the result must be `website_host + path`.
The existing parent-direction match must still return `website_host + path` (e.g. website `example.com`, instance `forum.example.com`).
Hosts that are unrelated or only share a non-dot-bounded suffix (e.g. `notexample.com` vs `example.com`) must still return the bare `website_host`.
The fix must stay within the else branch and return the same types as before (a String). The earlier equal-host and same-level-sibling branches are untouched.
items.notes: The finding matches the code: a 3-label website with a 2-label instance skips the line-144 branch and reaches line 149, where the check fails. Valid fixes include an OR of both directions, or a helper that checks either host ending with "." + the other. A plain `ends_with?(discourse_host)` without the dot boundary is a trap: it would wrongly match `notexample.com`. Separately, `"." << website_host` mutates a string literal and would raise under `frozen_string_literal`; replacing it with `+` is fine but not required.

items.defectStatement: `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (lines 98-116) changes the current user's `TopicUser.notification_level` and calls `save!` while handling a plain GET with no CSRF token, signed token or confirmation step. Any cross-site link or `` pointing at `/t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` silently lowers a logged-in victim's level to regular, and a second request (or a user already at regular) gets muted because the action toggles.
obligations: A cross-site GET without a valid anti-forgery credential must not change or save the user's notification level. Acceptable credentials are a Rails CSRF-protected non-GET request (POST/PUT) or a verified per-user signed/HMAC token tied to the user and topic.
When a legitimately authorized request arrives, the existing level logic must be preserved: above regular goes to regular, otherwise goes to muted, then the record is saved.

The slug-mismatch / blank-slug redirect to `unsubscribe_url` must still work, and a page must still render via `perform_show_response` (for example, a GET may render a confirmation page or the topic without mutating).
Any token check must be bound to `current_user` and the topic, compared in constant time or via `MessageVerifier`, and rejected when invalid or missing.
items.notes:
Several fixes are valid:
- Branch on request method (`request.get?` shows a confirmation or the topic; POST/PUT performs the mutation, relying on `protect_from_forgery` for non-GET).
- Verify a signed token from params before mutating.
Route changes and email-link generation are outside the cited lines; do not penalize a fix that assumes a POST route or a token parameter exists, as long as the action itself refuses unprotected GET mutation.

Traps that do not fix the issue:
- Checking `request.xhr?`, the Referer header, or `format.json` alone.
- Only moving the save after the redirect.

The nil `tu` crash (no `TopicUser` row) is a separate bug and is not required.

One caveat on the finding: Discourse's `before_filter` makes the action login-gated (per the diff), so it is an authenticated CSRF, as described.

items.defectStatement: The topic-unsubscribe route's model hook (lines 4-8) only calls PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id), which hits the normal topic JSON endpoint and never invokes the server unsubscribe action. A client-side transition to this route therefore shows the unsubscribe page while the user's notification level for the topic stays the same.
obligations: When the route is entered by a client-side transition, the server-side unsubscribe/notification-level change must actually be triggered, either by a request made in model() or by the page requiring an explicit submit. The page must not imply the user is unsubscribed when no change request was made.
The model hook must still resolve to a topic record (store-created topic updated from JSON), so afterModel's topic.set('details.notificationReasonText', null) and the template keep working.

Errors must still reject or propagate through the returned promise so route error handling works. If the unsubscribe request is chained, it must not run silently after a failure, or a failure must be surfaced.
items.notes: Valid fixes include: calling the unsubscribe endpoint (e.g. ajax to /t/:id/unsubscribe, or setting the notification level via the topic's details) before or alongside loadTopicView. Another valid fix is keeping the plain load and having the template require an explicit user action. The fix must stay within lines 4-8, so an explicit-submission approach would need supporting template or controller changes outside the cited lines. Graders should accept either approach only if the shown lines no longer present success without a state change. Using a JSON request to the unsubscribe URL that returns topic data is fine. The server endpoint name is not visible here, so do not penalize a reasonable choice of endpoint.

items.defectStatement: In add_members (lines 65-82), every username in the comma-separated list is looked up and passed to group.add without checking whether that user is already a member or appears twice in the list. Group#add pushes onto the has_many :through users association, which inserts a GroupUser row right away. A duplicate then violates the (group_id, user_id) uniqueness constraint and raises (e.g. ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique), giving a 500 instead of an idempotent success. Rows inserted before the failure stay committed.
obligations: Adding a username whose user is already a member of the group must not raise and must not create a second membership row.
A username repeated within one request must produce at most one membership.
Valid, non-member usernames must still be added. Unknown usernames must still be skipped silently. The automatic-group 422 guard and the success_json / render_json_error responses must be preserved.
A failure partway through must not leave some users added and others not (e.g. wrap the additions in a transaction), or else the loop must be made failure-free for the duplicate case.
items.notes: Valid ways to deduplicate include: uniq on the username list, checking group.users.include?/user_ids before adding, filtering with where.not(id: group.user_ids), or rescuing RecordNotUnique per user. Making Group#add itself idempotent is outside the cited lines, but a fix in the cited lines may rely on an equivalent check inline. The existence of the DB unique index cannot be confirmed from the shown code. Even without it, the fix still matters because duplicates would otherwise create duplicate join rows. A transaction is good practice, but the core defect is the missing duplicate/existing-member check. Don't fail a fix only for omitting the transaction if it removes every raise path. Stripping whitespace around usernames is an optional extra.

items.defectStatement: Line 17 makes the fallback chain depend on the runtime value of SiteSetting.default_locale. The finding says the translate_accelerator cache key is built only from key, config.locale and backend object_id. If so, translations that resolved through the old site locale stay cached after an admin changes default_locale, and users keep seeing stale fallback text.
obligations: After SiteSetting.default_locale changes, a lookup that falls back to the site locale must return text from the new default locale, not a cached result from the old one.
The fallback order must stay [requested locale, site default locale, :en], with duplicates and nils removed.
The fix must not clear or bypass the translation cache on every lookup. Invalidation (or a key change) should happen only when default_locale actually changes.
ensure_loaded! and existing callers of I18n.fallbacks[locale] must keep working and still return an array of locale symbols.
items.notes: The cache-key code (translate_accelerator in freedom_patches) is not shown, so the exact key format is the finding's claim and is unverified here. A fix confined to line 17 can only address the bug indirectly. One option is to remember the last-seen default_locale and invalidate the I18n/accelerator cache (e.g. a reload or cache clear) when it differs. Equally valid out-of-line fixes are adding default_locale to the cache key, or clearing the cache from a SiteSetting change hook. Credit any approach that ensures stale fallback text is not served without heavy per-call cost. Reject a fix that only reformats the fallback array, since it leaves the stale-cache problem unaddressed.

items.defectStatement: In EmbedController#best (lines 14-16), any request whose embed_url has no TopicEmbed record enqueues a :retrieve_topic job with no limit tied to the requester or to overall volume. The Referer check in ensure_embeddable is client-controlled, so unauthenticated clients can force unbounded job enqueues and the remote fetches and imports behind them by varying the URL.
obligations: Enqueueing :retrieve_topic from this branch must be bounded by a limit not keyed solely on the exact embed_url, such as per client IP, global, or per host. Once the limit is exceeded, no further jobs are enqueued.
Requests that stay within the limit must still enqueue :retrieve_topic with the same user_id and embed_url arguments and render 'loading'.
A rate-limited request must not raise an unhandled 500. Rendering 'loading' without enqueueing is acceptable, as is a controlled limit error.
The topic_id-found branch and the discourse_expires_in call must remain unchanged.
items.notes: Valid approaches include Discourse's RateLimiter (keyed on request.remote_ip or a global key) and a Redis counter or lock with a TTL. Rescuing RateLimiter::LimitExceeded is fine. The finding's suggestion to run PollFeed at most once per interval lives in TopicRetriever and Jobs::RetrieveTopic, outside the cited lines, so a fix here cannot be required to address it. The URL-keyed throttle is also not visible in the shown code. Rejecting embed_urls whose host differs from SiteSetting.embeddable_host is a reasonable extra check but does not satisfy the requirement alone, because distinct paths on that host still fan out. Simply moving the enqueue elsewhere without adding a limit does not fix the defect.

items.defectStatement: In absolutize_urls, the anchor check at lines 64-66 treats any href starting with '/' as root-relative. A protocol-relative href like `//cdn.example.com/a` has its leading slashes stripped and gets prefixed with the embed host, producing `http://embedhost/cdn.example.com/a` and breaking external links.
obligations: An href beginning with '//' (protocol-relative) must be left unchanged, or resolved to the external host. It must not be rewritten onto the embed host's path.
A root-relative href such as `/path/x` must still become `#{prefix}/path/x`.
Absolute hrefs (http/https/mailto etc.), relative hrefs without a leading slash, and blank/nil hrefs must stay unchanged.
items.notes: The cited lines cover only the <a> href loop. The identical img src bug at lines 70-72 is outside the cited range, so a fix for exactly these lines need not include it. Valid fixes include: excluding '//' with `!href.start_with?('//')`, using a regex like `/^\/(?!\/)/`, or prefixing protocol-relative URLs with `uri.scheme + ':'`. Using URI.join(url, href) is also acceptable if it keeps root-relative handling and does not raise on malformed hrefs.

items.defectStatement: In `.group-member-info .name` (line 497) the light-theme color was changed from the original `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` while wrapping it in `dark-light-choose`. This unintentionally lightens member names in the light theme. The change was meant only to add a dark-theme variant.
obligations: The light-theme (first) argument of `dark-light-choose` must restore `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`.
Keep the `dark-light-choose(...)` wrapper so a distinct dark-theme color still exists.
The dark-theme argument must be a `$secondary`-based scale-color that keeps names readable on dark backgrounds.
Leave the other declarations unchanged: display, margin-top, and vertical-align.
items.notes: The finding suggests a dark value of `$secondary` at 70% lightness, which mirrors 30%. Keeping the current `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)` is also acceptable. The defect is the light-theme value, not the dark one. Do not require any changes to `.title` or the other 50% lines; those matched their original values.

items.defectStatement: In mobile/modal.scss line 102, .custom-message-length previously used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%). The new dark-light-choose call gives the light theme $primary at 30% lightness instead of 70%, which changes the existing light-theme color to a much darker shade, and gives the dark theme $secondary at 70% instead of the mirrored 30%. Both arguments are inverted.
obligations: The light-theme (first) argument of dark-light-choose must be scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), preserving the original light-theme color.
The dark-theme (second) argument must use scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%), mirroring the light value.
Keep the dark-light-choose wrapper so dark-theme support remains, and leave the rest of the rule (margin, font-size) unchanged.
items.notes: The desktop/modal.scss comparison cannot be verified from the shown code, but the fix stands on the original value in the diff alone. Argument order is (light, dark). Reverting to plain scale-color without dark-light-choose loses the dark-theme intent and should not be accepted as the full fix.

items.defectStatement: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (no-arg, lines 64-71) passes both VIEW and MANAGE to hasPermission. hasPermission returns true if any listed scope is granted, so a subject holding only the all-groups VIEW scope passes canManage(). That lets a read-only group viewer perform group manage operations such as creating top-level groups.
obligations: The fallback permission check in canManage() must grant access only when the all-groups MANAGE scope is held; holding only VIEW must return false.
Preserve the early return of true for admins holding the MANAGE_USERS admin role (and do not add VIEW_USERS to that short-circuit).
Keep evaluating against the all-groups resource type, i.e. groupId null, as before.
items.notes: The fix is effectively `return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);`. Any equivalent that drops the VIEW scope is acceptable. The caller list in the finding (GroupsResource.createGroup and similar) is not visible in the shown code, but the defect is clear from the comparison with canManage(GroupModel) and canView(). Do not change hasPermission's any-of semantics, since that would break canView and the other methods that rely on it.

items.defectStatement: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() (lines 121-125), the loop uses groupResource.getId(), which is the internal authorization resource UUID, in two places. It is passed to hasPermission(), which looks the resource up with resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId) and so never finds the per-group resource; evaluation then falls back to the all-groups resource. It is also added to the returned set, so the set holds resource UUIDs instead of group ids and group-based user filtering matches no users. The group id is stored as the resource name, so groupResource.getName() must be used.
obligations: The value passed to hasPermission for each group resource must be the group id (the resource name, e.g. groupResource.getName()), so that findByName resolves the per-group resource.
The values added to the returned set must be group ids (the resource name), not resource UUIDs.
Keep the existing behavior: iterate GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE resources and check the VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS scopes.
An alternative fix that passes the Resource object directly to evaluation is acceptable, as long as the per-group resource is what gets evaluated and the returned set contains group ids.
items.notes: Both uses of getId() must be changed; a fix that changes only the granted.add call is incomplete. The type-level 'all-groups' resource may also be returned by findByType, since its name is the resource type. Filtering it out is a nice-to-have but not required. If it is not excluded, its name could end up in the set; at worst that is a harmless non-matching id.

items.defectStatement: getClientsWithPermission (lines 136-144) collects resources via findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE). In V2, per-client resources are looked up by name = client.getId() (see hasPermission(ClientModel, ...)) and are evidently not typed "Clients", so the query misses them. At most it hits the 'all-clients' type resource, whose name is the literal "Clients". The method therefore never returns real client identifiers and may return the bogus value "Clients", which breaks AvailableRoleMappingResource, the caller that treats the results as client IDs.
obligations: Must evaluate the per-client V2 resources (those named by the client's internal id) and include a client only when the requested scope is granted on that client's resource.

Returned values must be client identifiers in the form the caller expects, consistent with the V1 contract. They must never include the resource-type name "Clients" or other non-client resource names.
Preserve the existing early returns (emptySet when the admin is not same-realm or there is no realm resource server) and the use of hasGrantedPermission-style scope evaluation.
Must not throw or misbehave when a client has no dedicated resource; such clients are simply excluded, unless all-clients handling is deliberately added.
items.notes: The replacement is limited to lines 136-144, so the finding's first option (setting the type in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource) is not achievable there. Valid in-range approaches: iterate realm clients and use findByName(server, client.getId()); scan the server's resources and match names to existing clients; or filter out the type resource. The finding's 'map to client.getClientId()' needs checking against what the caller and V1 expect (internal id vs clientId). Accept either one if it matches the V1/caller contract; reject a fix that returns raw resource names without confirming they are client ids. Expanding an all-clients grant to every client is optional and not required.

items.defectStatement: In `canView(ClientModel)` (lines 78-79), the global `canView()` shortcut is evaluated first. That shortcut includes `hasPermission(VIEW)` against the all-clients resource, so an all-clients VIEW grant returns true before the concrete client's resource is ever evaluated. As a result, an explicit per-client VIEW denial is ignored and the admin can view the denied client.
obligations: When a per-client resource exists and its evaluation denies VIEW, an all-clients VIEW grant must not make `canView(client)` return true. The concrete client permission must be evaluated before, or instead of, the global all-clients VIEW shortcut.
Role-based access must keep short-circuiting to true: the view-clients and manage-clients admin roles via `canViewClientDefault()`.
Clients with no per-client resource and an all-clients VIEW grant must still be viewable. `hasPermission(client, VIEW)` already falls back to the all-clients resource in that case.
Clients the admin can configure or manage via `canConfigure(client)` must still be viewable.
items.notes: A typical valid fix replaces `canView()` with `canViewClientDefault()` in the shortcut and leaves the rest to `hasPermission(client, VIEW)`. Reordering so the per-client evaluation runs first is also acceptable, as long as an explicit denial wins. Trap: a fix that removes the role-based shortcut, or drops the all-clients fallback for clients without their own resource, is a regression. The finding's claim about `ClientsResource.getClients()` concerns code outside the cited lines and cannot be verified here, so do not require it. Whether all-clients grants are combined into per-client evaluation depends on the evaluator, which is not shown; graders should only require that an explicit per-client denial is not bypassed by the global shortcut.

items.defectStatement: In updateEvent, the fallback branch runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy, yet it searches event.destinationCalendar for a calendar whose externalId equals that falsy value. It essentially never matches, so selectedCalendar becomes undefined instead of the main destination calendar's externalId (the pre-change behavior). The update and the follow-up Meet patch then go out with no valid calendarId. The finding says the update targets "primary", but nothing in updateEvent defaults to "primary"; the value is simply undefined.
obligations: When externalCalendarId is truthy, selectedCalendar must still equal externalCalendarId unchanged.

When externalCalendarId is falsy, selectedCalendar must resolve to the main/first destination calendar's externalId (e.g. mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId or event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId), restoring the previous behavior.
It must not throw when event.destinationCalendar is null, undefined or an empty array.
items.notes: Matching by credentialId is not possible here because updateEvent receives no credentialId, so falling back to the first/main destination calendar is the expected fix. Adding a further `|| "primary"` default is acceptable but not required, since the old code had none. Equivalent expressions such as `externalCalendarId || mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` are valid. The same defect exists in deleteEvent (lines 315+), but that is outside the cited lines and should not be required.

items.defectStatement: In checkIfIsAvailable, when a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot falls inside it, lines 133-135 return true at once. The busy-time overlap check (busy.every at lines 153-180) is never reached, so slots that conflict with existing bookings or calendar events are reported as available.
obligations: When a date override exists for the day and the slot is within it, the slot must still be rejected if it overlaps any busy interval, using the same overlap logic as the existing busy.every check.
When a date override exists for the day, the working-hours check must still be skipped, because the override replaces normal working hours for that day.
Behavior must not change for: slots outside the override (still false), days with no override (working hours then busy check), and the currentSeats early return.
items.notes: Several fixes are valid: return busy.every(...) instead of true, or skip the working-hours block when dateOverrideExist and fall through to the busy check. A trap is simply deleting lines 133-135: override days would then also be filtered by working hours, which is wrong. Other bugs in the window are out of scope for this finding, e.g. the === comparison of dayjs objects at line 114 and end computed the same as start at line 142.

items.defectStatement: At line 1078, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently does nothing when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`. That happens when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar (lines 1063-1067). In that case the collective team members' destination calendars are dropped, and their calendars never receive the event.
obligations: For COLLECTIVE team events where `evt.destinationCalendar` is null and `teamDestinationCalendars` is non-empty, `evt.destinationCalendar` must end up as an array containing all of `teamDestinationCalendars`.
When `evt.destinationCalendar` is already an array, the existing entries (event-type or organizer calendar) must stay first, with the team calendars appended after them in order.
Non-collective or non-team events must not be affected: no team calendars added and no change to `destinationCalendar`.
items.notes: Valid fixes include `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`, or initializing to `[]` and then pushing. Leaving the value `null` when `teamDestinationCalendars` is empty is acceptable and arguably safer, since downstream code may test truthiness. Converting null to an empty array is also acceptable, because the booking `connect` check tests `length > 0`. A fix that only changes the `?.` operator without handling null (for example a non-null assertion) would throw at runtime and is wrong. As a side effect, with no organizer calendar, `evt.destinationCalendar[0]` (used for the booking's `connect` at ~1875) becomes the first team member's calendar; that is expected, not a defect.

items.defectStatement: `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` in GroupPermissionsV2 collects `groupResource.getId()`, the internal authorization resource ID, instead of the group ID. V2 group resources are named by group ID, which is how `hasPermission` looks them up via `findByName`. So the returned set (and the `hasPermission` lookup inside the loop) does not hold real group IDs, and downstream user search/count filtering by these IDs cannot match members of V2-permitted groups. The finding further claims the JPA `groupsWithPermissionsSubquery` only matches legacy `group.resource.<groupId>` names; that consumer is not shown here.
obligations: The set returned at line 127 must contain actual group IDs, i.e. the V2 resource names, not authorization resource internal IDs, for every group where VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS is granted.
Group IDs in the returned set must be in the form the user search/count consumer can match against V2 resources; returning raw resource IDs is not acceptable.
Existing early returns must be preserved: an empty set when the admin can view all users, is not in the same realm, or has no realm resource server.
The type-level 'all groups' resource must not be emitted as if it were a group ID.
items.notes: The cited range is only `return granted;`. The real root cause is that line 123 (and the `hasPermission` argument on line 122) uses `getId()` instead of `getName()`. A fix confined to line 127 could map the collected resource IDs to their names, for example via `findById(...).getName()`. However, the per-group permission check on line 122 would still look up by the wrong key, so graders should accept either approach or note the partial fix. Updating the JPA subquery contract, as the finding suggests, is outside the cited lines and the shown code; it cannot be verified here. Treat the legacy-name claim as unverified context, not a requirement for this replacement.

items.defectStatement: In scheduleSMSReminders.ts lines 178-186, the new else branch increments retryCount whenever twilio.scheduleSMS returns a falsy value. That includes the case where the user or team is SMS-locked and scheduleSMS deliberately returns undefined. The new deleteMany condition (retryCount > 1) then permanently deletes these still-valid reminders after two cron runs, so they are never sent once the lock is lifted.
obligations: A falsy/undefined return from scheduleSMS caused by an SMS lock must not increment retryCount, and must not otherwise make the reminder eligible for the retryCount-based deletion.
The reminder must stay unscheduled (scheduled not set to true) so a later cron run can retry it after the lock is lifted.
The successful path (scheduled: true, referenceId set) and the catch-block retryCount increment for genuine errors must be preserved.
items.notes: The simplest valid fix removes the else branch entirely. An alternative is to distinguish the lock case explicitly, for example by checking the lock state or by having scheduleSMS signal it, and only increment for other falsy results. The fix is limited to the cited lines, so changing twilioProvider is out of scope. A fix should not be credited if it merely changes the increment amount or moves the same unconditional increment elsewhere.

items.defectStatement: Line 118 sets `mainHostDestinationCalendar` to undefined when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or an empty array. Line 119 then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without a guard, so `create()` throws a TypeError. Because `&&` short-circuits, this only happens when `evt.location === MeetLocationType` (Google Meet). In that case event creation aborts instead of falling back to Cal Video.
obligations: When `evt.destinationCalendar` is null, undefined, or an empty array and the location is Google Meet, `create()` must not throw.
In that case the location must be set to "integrations:daily", matching the pre-PR behavior where `undefined !== "google_calendar"` triggered the fallback.
When the first destination calendar's integration is "google_calendar", the Meet location must be kept unchanged.
When the first destination calendar has any other integration, the fallback to "integrations:daily" must still happen; non-Meet locations must be unaffected.
items.notes: Valid fixes include optional chaining (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`), indexing with `evt.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.integration`, or an explicit existence check. A trap is a guard that skips the fallback when no calendar exists, e.g. `mainHostDestinationCalendar && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== ...`: it avoids the crash but leaves Meet set with no Google calendar, which reverses the intended behavior. The finding overstates the scope slightly, since the crash only occurs for the Google Meet location, not for every event creation.

items.defectStatement: On line 151 the condition for spreading `slug` into the organization create data was inverted from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`. When billing is enabled, the org slug is now set immediately, bypassing the requestedSlug/payment flow. When billing is disabled, the org is created with no slug at all.
obligations: `slug` must be set on the organization create data only when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is false, and omitted when it is true.
The metadata `requestedSlug: slug` must still be added only when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true (line 153 behavior preserved).
The other metadata fields (isOrganization, isOrganizationVerified, isOrganizationConfigured, orgAutoAcceptEmail) and `name` must be unchanged.
items.notes: Line 153 is correct as written. The ternary form is equivalent to the original `&&` spread, so it must not be flipped. Either `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` or `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` is a valid fix. Exactly one of slug / requestedSlug should be present for any given flag value.

items.defectStatement: parseRefreshTokenResponse always sets the literal placeholder `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when the parsed response has no refresh_token, including in the normal (non-sharing) branch that uses the caller's schema. Callers like office365calendar spread the parsed data over their stored credentials and persist the result. A provider response that omits refresh_token then overwrites the real stored refresh token with the placeholder, and every later refresh fails.
obligations: In the non-sharing branch (parsed with the caller's `schema`), a response without refresh_token must not come back with a fabricated refresh_token value. The field must stay absent/undefined so that a caller's spread keeps the existing stored token.
Responses that do include a refresh_token must be returned unchanged.

The credential-sharing/sync branch (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, minimumTokenResponseSchema) may keep injecting the placeholder, so that callers whose schemas require refresh_token still work there.
Invalid responses must still throw, and the function must still return the safeParse result object.
items.notes: Valid fixes include: limiting the injection to the sharing/sync branch, or adding an opt-in parameter that callers set. Removing the injection entirely is also acceptable for this finding, though it may break sharing-mode callers that require refresh_token; graders should accept it but may mention that risk. A fix that only rewrites lines 25-27 can refer to the branch condition, either by re-checking the env/constant or by using a flag; the latter needs line 15 or a variable that is not shown. The CalendarService line references come from the finding and cannot be verified here, but the spread-and-persist mechanism is plausible.

items.defectStatement: The single try/catch wraps the whole cancellation loop (lines 53-77), so one rejected SendGrid `client.request` (bad, null or already-cancelled batch_id) exits the loop. The remaining cancelled reminders are never cancelled at SendGrid, and the already-collected `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` calls never run, because Prisma promises are lazy and `Promise.all` is skipped. As a result, emails for cancelled or rescheduled bookings can still be sent, and a persistently failing reminder early in the list blocks the others on every cron run.
obligations: A failure cancelling one reminder at SendGrid must not stop the remaining reminders in `remindersToCancel` from being cancelled.
Every reminder whose SendGrid cancel succeeded must have its workflowReminder DB delete actually executed and awaited, even if other reminders failed.
Errors must still be caught and logged rather than thrown, so the handler goes on to the unscheduled-reminder scheduling section and still responds.
The SendGrid request payload must stay the same: `/v3/user/scheduled_sends`, POST, with `batch_id` set to `referenceId` and status `cancel`.
items.notes: Valid fixes include a per-iteration try/catch, `Promise.allSettled` over per-reminder tasks, or sequential versus parallel processing. Whether a reminder whose cancel failed is kept for retry or deleted anyway is a judgment call; either is acceptable as long as successful ones get deleted. The finding says the pushed deletes are "never awaited"; more precisely, Prisma delete promises are lazy, so they never execute at all. A fix that awaits each delete inline is fine.

items.defectStatement: In `create()`'s `referencesToCreate` mapping (line 170), the non-calendar branch of `credentialId` was changed from `result.credentialId` to `undefined`. Booking references for video results (e.g. Daily/Zoom) therefore lose the credential id needed later to update or delete that video meeting.
obligations: For non-calendar (video) results, `credentialId` must again be `result.credentialId`.
For calendar results, `credentialId` must remain `result.credentialId`.
`externalCalendarId` must stay `result.externalId` for calendar results and `undefined` otherwise. The cited line 169 needs no behavioral change.
items.notes: The simplest valid fix is an unconditional `credentialId: result.credentialId`; a redundant ternary is also acceptable. Do not require restoring `evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId`, because `destinationCalendar` is now an array and the per-result credentialId is the correct source. Line 169 is not a defect.

items.defectStatement: At lines 70-77 the blacklist entries are lowercased, but each guest is compared raw with `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. A blocked address therefore passes the filter if it differs only in case (e.g. `Blocked@x.com`) or uses a plus-alias (`blocked+1@x.com`), and gets added as an attendee.
obligations: The blacklist comparison must be case-insensitive: a guest that differs from a blacklist entry only by letter case must be filtered out.

Plus-addressed variants of a blacklisted address (e.g. `user+tag@domain` when `user@domain` is blacklisted) must be filtered out, consistent with base-email normalization such as `extractBaseEmail(...).toLowerCase()`.
Non-blacklisted guests must still pass. Guests already in `booking.attendees` must still be excluded. An empty or unset `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` must block nothing.
Normalization should apply only to the comparison. Guests that pass the filter should keep their original address for storage, unless the fix deliberately changes that.
items.notes: `extractBaseEmail` is not imported in this file, so a fix that uses it needs an import outside the cited lines. Equivalent inline normalization (lowercase plus stripping the `+tag` from the local part) is also acceptable. Optionally, the blacklist entries can be trimmed and normalized the same way, which helps with spaces after commas. Making the attendee-duplicate check case-insensitive is a bonus, not required. The plus-alias parity with handleNewBooking cannot be verified from the shown code; accept it as the stated intent. Separate issue outside the cited lines: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` uses the unfiltered `guests`, so blacklisted addresses still get emailed. Do not penalize a fix for not addressing this.

items.defectStatement: At line 114 two freshly created Dayjs objects are compared with `===`. That is reference equality, so the check is always false. A date override whose start equals its end (the representation of a full day marked unavailable) is therefore never caught by this branch. Such a slot can be judged available, either by falling through to `dateOverrideExist` → true or by slipping past the before/after checks at 117-125.
obligations: The start/end equality check must compare time values (e.g. `isSame`, `valueOf()`, or `getTime()`), not object references. It must return true (slot excluded) when the override's start and end represent the same instant.
When start and end differ, the condition must stay false, so non-empty overrides still fall through to the existing before/after range checks.
The early `return true` inside the find callback must be preserved, along with the surrounding `dateOverrideExist` behavior.
items.notes: Equivalent valid fixes include comparing `date.start.getTime() === date.end.getTime()`, comparing the raw Dates via `dayjs(date.start).isSame(dayjs(date.end))`, or using the offset-adjusted values with `isSame`. Adding the same utcOffset to both sides does not change whether they are equal. Comparing `.format()` strings at minute or ms precision is also acceptable if the precision is sufficient. Using `==` is not a fix, because it still compares references.

items.defectStatement: In the recurring 'cancel all remaining' branch (lines 449-457), the loop over each outer calendar reference ignores the credential it resolved (`calendarCredential`/`calendar`). Instead it iterates all of the organizer's calendar credentials and deletes only the first `_calendar` reference of each updated booking. As a result, co-host references on collective bookings, whose credentials come from the DB lookup, are never deleted. The organizer's first-reference deletes are also repeated once per outer reference and once per organizer calendar credential.
obligations: For each outer reference with a resolved credential, delete, in every updated occurrence, the reference(s) that correspond to that credential (e.g., matching `credentialId`, or type/credential), using that resolved credential's calendar. Do not use the organizer's other credentials.

Co-host (non-organizer) calendar events of recurring collective bookings must be deleted. The organizer's events must still be deleted, and each occurrence's event must not be deleted repeatedly across iterations.
Preserve pushing results/promises into `apiDeletes`, the error logging around the recurring deletes, and the non-recurring single-delete path.
items.notes: Matching by `credentialId` on `updBooking.references` is natural, since the select includes `credentialId`. Matching by externalCalendarId/type plus credential is also acceptable if it is unambiguous. An alternative valid fix is to restructure so that each occurrence's references are each deleted via their own credential. The fix may need to touch lines 458-461 (closing of the map) as well. Legacy references without a `credentialId` are out of scope.

items.defectStatement: Lines 46-48 join the isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner checks with `&&`, so `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is true only when the user holds both roles. A team admin who is not an owner (or an owner, if isTeamOwner does not also count as admin) who is neither the organizer nor an attendee is wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN.
obligations: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` must be true when the user is a team admin OR a team owner of the booking's event type team; either role alone is enough.
Both checks must still use the booking's team id with the same `?? 0` fallback, so bookings without a team do not grant team privileges.
The variable name and its boolean meaning must stay the same, so the FORBIDDEN check on line 54 keeps working with the organizer and attendee checks unchanged.
Users who are neither admin nor owner must still evaluate to false.
items.notes: Valid fixes include `||` with short-circuit evaluation, running both checks via Promise.all and OR-ing the results, or a single combined membership query. Any of these is fine if the result is the logical OR. isTeamAdmin/isTeamOwner may return a membership object or null rather than a boolean; a truthy value is acceptable because it is only used in a negated condition.

items.defectStatement: createEvent always takes the first entry of event.destinationCalendar (the main host's) to build the events URL. For collective bookings where EventManager calls it with a co-host's Office365 credential, it POSTs to the organizer's calendar ID using the co-host's token. That calendar is not accessible under /me for the co-host, so the co-host's event creation fails or lands in the wrong place.
obligations: When createEvent is called for a given credential, the target calendar must be the destinationCalendar entry whose credentialId matches that credential, not unconditionally the first entry.
If no destinationCalendar entry matches the credential (or none exist or there is no externalId), fall back to the default `/me/calendar/events` endpoint rather than using another host's calendar ID.
Preserve existing behavior for single-host bookings: when the main host's credential is used, still post to `/me/calendars/{externalId}/events` for its destination calendar.
items.notes: Valid fixes include accepting an optional credentialId parameter in createEvent (as CalendarManager passes it) or storing the credential id from the constructor and matching against it; either approach is fine. A fix touching only lines 73-76 may need the credential id to be available, for example from a field captured in the constructor. Do not accept a fix that just picks a different fixed index. The updateEvent/deleteEvent paths are out of scope.

items.defectStatement: In checkIfIsAvailable (lines 105-131), the `dateOverrides.find` callback returns true for the first same-day override the slot falls outside of, and that result rejects the slot. With several overrides on one day (e.g. 09:00-11:00 and 14:00-16:00), a 14:30 slot is outside the first override, so `find` returns true and the function returns false, even though the slot lies inside the second override. The `dateOverrideExist` flag is set as a side effect of the same callback.
obligations: When one or more overrides fall on the slot's day, the slot must be rejected only if it fits in none of them. A slot inside any same-day override must not be rejected by this block; it should reach the `dateOverrideExist` → `return true` path.

`dateOverrideExist` (or an equivalent) must still be true whenever any override matches the slot's day, so working hours are skipped for override days. When no override matches the day, behavior must fall through to the working-hours and busy checks unchanged.
Preserve the per-override organizer timezone offset conversion (`utcOffset` via `organizerTimeZone`) and the YYYY MM DD day matching when comparing override bounds to the slot.

A zero-length override (start equals end, meaning unavailable that day) must still make slots that day unavailable. The existing boundary semantics must be kept: a slot ending at or before the override start is outside, and a slot starting after the override end is outside.
items.notes:
Valid fixes include filtering the same-day overrides first and then using `.some`/`.every` for containment, or a loop that tracks whether any match. Grader traps:
- Line 114 compares Dayjs objects with `===`, which is always false. A fix that keeps it is not wrong for this finding, but should not rely on it. Using `isSame`/`valueOf` there is an acceptable improvement.
- The existing check does not require the slot end to be at or before the override end. Adding that is optional and should not be required.
- Do not penalize a fix that leaves the working-hours code (lines 138-151) untouched, since it is out of scope.

items.defectStatement: In the catch block (lines 189-196), retryCount is written as the absolute value `reminder.retryCount + 1`, computed from the row read at the start of the cron run. If another run or update increments the same reminder in the meantime, this write overwrites it and retries are undercounted. The `retryCount > 1` deletion cleanup then fires later than intended.
obligations: The catch-block update must increment retryCount relative to the current database value rather than a stale in-memory value, e.g. Prisma `retryCount: { increment: 1 }`.
It must still target only the failing reminder (`where: { id: reminder.id }`) and must not change other fields.
The update must remain inside the catch block. Error logging must still happen, and the loop must continue to the next reminder.
items.notes: Prisma `{ increment: 1 }` is the natural fix. A raw SQL `retryCount = retryCount + 1` is also acceptable. The race only matters if cron runs overlap, so the severity is modest, but the bug is real. The same pattern exists in the else branch at lines 179-186, which is outside the cited lines; a fix need not touch it. A fix that also wraps the update in try/catch, so a failing update does not abort the loop, is fine but not required.

items.defectStatement: In checkIfIsAvailable (lines 138-151), `workingHours.find` returns the first working-hours entry for the slot's UTC weekday that does not contain the slot, and the function then returns false. With several ranges on one day (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00), every slot falls outside at least one range, so all slots are rejected. Fixed hosts with split working days therefore lose all availability. Separately, `end` is computed from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, so the end bound is never really checked.
obligations: A slot must be rejected only when none of the working-hours entries that apply to its weekday contains it. A slot inside any one applicable range (e.g. 10:00 or 14:00 with ranges 09-12 and 13-17) must pass on to the busy-time check.
A slot outside every applicable range (e.g. 12:30 with ranges 09-12 and 13-17) must still return false.
The default `workingHours = []` must not cause every slot to be rejected. The empty case must keep passing through to the busy check as it does today.
The date-override handling above and the busy-time check below must stay unchanged.
items.notes: The finding is correct. Its suggested `!workingHours.some(...)` would reject everything when workingHours is empty, and would reject days that have no matching entry, which the current code allows. A fix that guards on 'some entry applies to this day' (or on a non-empty list) is safer, though rejecting days with no entries is arguably acceptable if the empty-list case is preserved. Computing `end` from slotEndTime is a welcome correction but should not be required. If it is done, watch for slots that cross UTC midnight, where end minutes wrap. The existing comparison mixes the start/end semantics and that should not be penalized beyond these points.

items.defectStatement: In checkIfIsAvailable's working-hours check (lines 138-151), `end` is computed from `slotStartTime`, so a slot that runs past a working-hour entry's endTime is accepted. The `find` also rejects the slot if any single same-day entry fails to contain it, so a host with several disjoint entries on one day (e.g. 9-12 and 13-17) has every slot rejected.
obligations: The end bound must come from the slot's end (slotEndTime, or start + eventLength in minutes), so a slot that starts inside an entry but ends after its endTime is rejected.

A slot is accepted by this check if at least one working-hour entry for that day fully contains [start, end]. It must not be rejected just because some other entry on the same day does not contain it (e.g. with entries 9-12 and 13-17, a 10:00-10:30 slot and a 14:00-15:00 slot both pass).

Existing behavior must be preserved: when workingHours is empty (the default), the check rejects nothing. Rejection still returns false before the busy check, and the start-time bound (start < startTime) is still enforced.
items.notes: The finding is accurate. Trap: computing end as slotEndTime.hour()*60+minute() wraps to 0 when a slot ends exactly at midnight UTC (or crosses it), making end < start. Accept `end = start + eventLength` or an equivalent that handles this; flag a pure hour/minute version as a weaker fix. Two treatments of a day with no matching entries are acceptable: keep accepting the slot (current behavior, and consistent with the finding's 'no entry on that day' wording), or reject it. Do not fail a fix over that choice, but it must not reject everything when workingHours is empty. Using `some`, filter+every, or a loop are all valid.

items.defectStatement: In the per-reminder catch block (lines 189-197), the newly added `prisma.workflowReminder.update` that increments retryCount is not guarded. If it throws (record deleted concurrently, P2025 not-found, or a transient DB error), the exception escapes the catch and aborts the for loop. The remaining reminders are then never processed, the handler never sends its 200 response, and the original error is never logged.
obligations: A failure of the retryCount update inside the catch block must not propagate out of the loop iteration. Processing must continue with the next reminder, and the handler must still reach `res.status(200)`.
The original scheduling error must still be logged even when the retryCount update fails.
When the update succeeds, it must still increment retryCount by 1 for the failed reminder (same where/data semantics).
items.notes: Valid fixes include wrapping the update in its own try/catch (optionally logging the update failure), or using `.catch(...)` on the update promise. Moving the console.log before the update alone is insufficient: it preserves the log but the update error would still abort the loop. The else-branch update at lines 179-186 has a similar issue, but it sits inside the try, so its errors go to this catch; that is outside the cited lines. Swallowing the update error silently is acceptable as long as the original error is still logged.

items.defectStatement: The recurring-series branch (lines 444-461) runs inside the per-calendar-reference loop. On every iteration it deletes each updated booking's first `_calendar` reference through every organizer `_calendar` credential. With N calendar references the same events are deleted N times (times the number of organizer credentials), duplicates fail, and references belonging to other hosts' credentials are never deleted with the correct credential.
obligations: When a recurring series is cancelled with allRemainingBookings, each updated booking's calendar event must be deleted once per matching reference, not repeated for every outer reference iteration.

Deletion for a given reference must use that reference's credential (e.g. the already-resolved `calendarCredential`/`calendar`, matched by credentialId on the updated booking's references), not every organizer credential. This lets other hosts' events be deleted through their own credentials.

The replacement must still define `promises` as something `Promise.all` can await, and must keep the `if (...) {` opening, because lines 462-471 (try/await Promise.all(promises)/catch and the else branch for non-recurring single deletes) are unchanged.
The non-recurring path and the legacy no-credentialId path must keep working as before. Deleted results must still be pushed to apiDeletes.
items.notes: Since only lines 444-461 can be replaced, the natural fix is to scope deletion to the current reference: for each updated booking, find the reference with the same credentialId (or matching type/externalCalendarId) and delete it via the current `calendar`. Moving the bulk delete outside the loop is also valid in principle but hard to do within the cited range. A fix that just guards with a 'run once' flag but still uses all organizer credentials only partly fixes the problem, because other hosts' events stay undeleted. Using `.find` for only the first `_calendar` reference per updated booking is part of the defect.

items.defectStatement: Lines 216-224 shift the override by the organizer-to-invitee offset, then keep only the time of day (`hour()*60+minute()`). Any override that crosses midnight after the shift wraps around. A shifted range can land on the wrong part of the invitee's day (e.g. 20:00-23:00 +6h → 02:00-05:00 on the original day), or come out with endTime < startTime, which yields misplaced slots or no slots.
obligations: startTime/endTime must keep the day boundary crossed by the shift, e.g. as minutes relative to the invitee day that may be negative or ≥1440, or by clamping/splitting at midnight. They must not be reduced modulo 24h.
A shifted override that spans midnight must not produce endTime < startTime, and must not produce a range moved to the wrong part of the day.
Overrides that do not cross midnight after the shift must produce the same startTime/endTime values as now, including the same organizer→invitee offset semantics.
The userIds field and the returned TimeFrame shape must be preserved.
items.notes: The finding's suggested `dayjs(override.start).tz(timeZone).diff(startOfInviteeDay)` is not automatically correct. The previous code read override wall-clock time from the UTC fields (getUTCHours), so applying `.tz(timeZone)` directly may double-convert. Accept any fix that applies the existing offset and measures from the correct invitee-day base without wrapping. Clamping or splitting at day boundaries is also acceptable. How buildSlots handles values outside 0-1440 is not visible here, so a fix that relies on out-of-range minutes should be judged plausible rather than proven. The duplicated dayjs calls are only a style issue.

items.defectStatement: In `getClient` (lines 75-99) every SalesforceCalendarService construction POSTs directly to login.salesforce.com with Cal.com's own consumer key/secret and then writes to the DB. Because it bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`, the credential-sync endpoint is ignored when sync is enabled. The success check `response.statusText !== "OK"` also rejects valid 200 responses whose statusText is empty (e.g. HTTP/2) or not exactly "OK".
obligations: Success/failure of the token refresh must be decided by HTTP status (e.g. `response.ok` / status code), not by `statusText`; a 200 with an empty statusText must not throw.

The refresh call must go through `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` (with app slug "salesforce" and the credential's userId) or otherwise honor credential sync, so the sync endpoint is used when it is enabled.

Preserve the existing behavior on a successful refresh: validate the response with `parseRefreshTokenResponse`/`salesforceTokenSchema`, reject on invalid tokens, and persist the new key while keeping the existing `refresh_token`.

Avoid an unconditional refresh round trip and DB write on every client creation. Either refresh only when needed (token missing/invalid/expired) or leave it to jsforce's built-in refresh via `refreshToken`.
items.notes: Salesforce token responses carry `issued_at` but no `expires_in`, so a strict expiry check is not directly available. Valid conditional strategies include: refreshing only when `access_token` is missing; refreshing on an auth error; or dropping the eager refresh and relying on jsforce's auto-refresh (optionally persisting via its `refresh` event). Do not penalize a fix for not computing exact expiry. `refreshOAuthTokens` is not currently imported in the shown file, so a fix may need an import outside the cited lines; accept that. Related issue outside the cited range: the jsforce Connection at lines 101-108 still uses the old `credentialKey.access_token`/`instance_url`, not the refreshed values, so the current refresh is effectively wasted. A fix that also feeds the refreshed token into the connection is good but not required by this finding. When sync is enabled, the response shape from the sync endpoint may differ, and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` already handles that.

items.defectStatement: `selectedCalendar` (lines 147-149) is now `undefined` when no destination calendar matches `credentialId`, including when `destinationCalendar` is empty. Only the insert call applies the `|| "primary"` fallback, so the later `calendar.events.patch` (line 168) receives `calendarId: undefined`. That patch fails (unhandled, fire-and-forget), and the event description never gets the Google Meet hangout link. Before this diff, `selectedCalendar` itself defaulted to "primary", so this is a regression.
obligations: When no destination calendar matches `credentialId` (empty or undefined `destinationCalendar`, or no match), the calendarId later used by the hangout-link patch must be "primary", not undefined.
The insert call must still target the matching calendar's externalId when one exists, and "primary" otherwise.
Calendar selection must still match the destination calendar by `credentialId`. Do not revert to just taking the first entry.
Insert and patch must resolve to the same calendar.
items.notes: The patch call at line 168 is outside the cited range. A fix limited to lines 145-154 therefore has to make the fallback part of the resolved variable, e.g. `const selectedCalendar = ...?.externalId || "primary"` (or `?? "primary"`). Keeping the `|| "primary"` at the insert call then becomes redundant but harmless. Introducing a new resolved variable that is used only at the insert does not fix the patch call, and the grader should reject it unless line 168 also changes.

items.defectStatement: Line 31 calls `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` without any error handling. A body with a missing or invalid userId, appSlug or keys throws an uncaught ZodError. The authenticated caller then gets a generic 500 (or a framework error) instead of a 400 client-error response.
obligations: A malformed or invalid request body must cause the handler to return a 4xx response (400 expected) with a JSON message, and it must return early without reaching the prisma or decrypt logic.
A valid body must still produce a typed `reqBody` with userId, appSlug and keys, so the later code (lines 34-91) keeps working unchanged.
The handler must not throw an uncaught ZodError for invalid input.
items.notes: Valid fixes include `safeParse` with an early `return res.status(400)`, or a try/catch around `parse` that catches ZodError and returns 400. Including the zod issues in the response is optional. The finding says the error 'leaks the exception path', which is overstated: Next.js returns a generic 500 in production. The request is already secret-authenticated, so this is about the error contract, not security. Other unhandled throws, such as JSON.parse or decrypt on line 57, are outside the cited line and are not required.

items.defectStatement: In packages/app-store/index.ts lines 1-31, every app entry is a bare `import("./x")` call inside the object literal. All of them therefore run as soon as the module is evaluated, and every app module and its heavy dependencies (Google, Office365, Stripe, etc.) start loading on import of `@calcom/app-store`. The switch to dynamic imports defers nothing; it only turns each value into a Promise.
obligations: Each appStore entry must not start loading its module when index.ts is evaluated. Loading must be deferred until a specific app is requested, for example by making each value a function that returns `import("./x")`.
Preserve the full set of 28 app keys with the same names, each mapped to its correct module path.
Keep `export default appStore` and an object keyed by app slug, so callers can still look up by key. Requesting an app must still resolve to its module namespace.
items.notes: Valid alternatives include per-key thunks, a getter, or a lookup function such as a switch keyed by slug. The essential test is that no `import()` executes at module top level. Use sites outside the cited lines (`appStore[key]` → `appStore[key]?.()`) would also need updating, but they are not part of this replacement, so do not penalize a fix for not showing them. Keeping static top-level imports would be a regression, since it still loads everything eagerly. Simply removing `import()` without deferral also fails.

items.defectStatement: In deleteScheduledSMSReminder (lines 177-186), the prisma.workflowReminder.delete runs after twilio.cancelSMS in the same try block. If cancelSMS throws, the delete is skipped and the error is only logged, leaving an orphaned workflowReminder row. Before this diff, the caller deleted that row independently of the Twilio result.
obligations: When referenceId is non-null and twilio.cancelSMS throws or rejects, the workflowReminder row for reminderId must still be deleted (or otherwise reliably handled, e.g. marked cancelled), not skipped.
twilio.cancelSMS must still be called when referenceId is non-null and must not be called when referenceId is null; the DB delete must still happen in the null case.
The function must keep its (reminderId: number, referenceId: string | null) signature and must not throw to callers: errors from Twilio and from Prisma must still be caught and logged.
items.notes: Valid fixes include: a separate try/catch around cancelSMS followed by the delete; putting the delete in a finally block (it still needs its own error handling so the function doesn't throw); or Promise.allSettled. Marking the row cancelled instead of deleting it is acceptable only if the row is no longer treated as active. The finding overstates the impact. Rows with a referenceId are already scheduled on Twilio's side, so the SMS gets sent because cancelSMS failed, not because the DB row survives. Deleting the row does not stop that send. The concrete defect is the orphaned or stale DB row and the regression from the previous behavior. Adding Twilio retry logic is optional and not required.

items.defectStatement: `deleteCacheMutation` (lines 42-50) only shows a toast and calls the optional parent `onSuccess`; it never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. If the parent does not refetch, the `cacheUpdatedAt` prop stays stale after a successful cache deletion, so the dropdown keeps showing the old cache status and delete option. `disconnectMutation` does invalidate this query.
obligations: After a successful `deleteCache` mutation (or on settle), `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` (or an equivalent tRPC utils handle) must be invalidated so `cacheUpdatedAt` refreshes without relying on the parent.
The success toast (`cache_deleted_successfully`) and the call to the optional parent `onSuccess?.()` must be kept.
The error toast (`error_deleting_cache`) on failure must be kept.
The replacement must compile in place: it must not redeclare `const utils` in the cited lines, because `utils` is already declared at line 52 outside the cited range.
items.notes: Referencing `utils` from line 52 inside the mutation callback is fine. The callback runs after render, so there is no temporal-dead-zone issue and TS does not flag it. Calling a separate `trpc.useUtils()` under a different name is also acceptable. Invalidating in `onSuccess` or in `onSettled` are both valid; awaiting the invalidation is optional. Also invalidating `apps.integrations` is optional, not required. Making the parent `onSuccess` refetch is not a valid fix, because it lies outside the cited lines and leaves the component dependent on the parent.

items.defectStatement: The `guests` field in ZAddGuestsInputSchema (lines 3-6) is `z.array(z.string().email())` and does not enforce uniqueness. A client can submit the same email more than once, and duplicate attendee records may be created downstream.
obligations: Server-side validation must reject or deduplicate duplicate emails in `guests`, so the parsed output never contains the same email twice.
Valid inputs must keep their current behavior: `bookingId` stays a number, each guest must still be a valid email, and an array of distinct emails passes unchanged.
The exported schema must remain usable as a tRPC input, and `TAddGuestsInputSchema` must still infer `guests` as `string[]`.
items.notes: Two fixes are valid: `.refine()` rejecting duplicates, or `.transform()` deduplicating (e.g. via a Set). Case-insensitive comparison (lowercasing) is a reasonable improvement but not required. The handler code is not shown, so the claim about createMany inserting duplicates cannot be verified; the handler may already filter against existing attendees. Treat the impact as plausible, not confirmed. The fix may only touch lines 3-6.

items.defectStatement: In the date-override check (lines 117-124), a slot is rejected only if it ends at or before the override start, or starts strictly after the override end. As a result, slots that partially overlap the override still pass. For a 10:00–11:00 override, 09:30–10:30, 10:30–11:30 and a slot starting exactly at 11:00 are all wrongly treated as available.
obligations: The find callback must return true (slot not within override → unavailable) whenever slotStartTime is before the offset-adjusted override start or slotEndTime is after the offset-adjusted override end.

A slot fully contained in the override, including one that starts exactly at the override start or ends exactly at the override end, must not be rejected; it should fall through and leave the slot available.
The existing `dayjs(date.X).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` adjustment must be applied to both bounds so timezone handling is preserved.
Control flow must be kept intact: return true to reject, otherwise fall through so the callback returns undefined. dateOverrideExist and the surrounding logic must stay unchanged.
items.notes: Equivalent forms are all valid, e.g. `slotStartTime.isBefore(start) || slotEndTime.isAfter(end)`, or a negated `isSameOrAfter`/`isSameOrBefore` containment check. The existing `slotEnd <= start` check becomes redundant and may be dropped or kept. Several issues sit outside the cited lines and should not be required: the `===` comparison at line 114 is always false; multiple overrides on the same day are not handled, since any one failing override rejects the slot; and the working-hours `end` at line 142 is computed from the start time. Do not penalize a fix for ignoring these.

items.defectStatement: In the uniqueGuests filter (lines 74-78), both comparisons are case-sensitive. The attendee check uses `guest === attendee.email`, so an existing attendee can be re-added with different casing. The blacklist is lowercased on line 71 but checked against the raw guest string, so any guest email containing uppercase letters (e.g. `Bad@X.com`) bypasses a blacklisted `bad@x.com`.
obligations: A guest whose email matches an existing attendee's email ignoring case must be filtered out.
A guest whose email matches a blacklisted email ignoring case must be filtered out, including when the guest input has uppercase letters.

Guests that differ from every attendee and every blacklist entry (case-insensitively) must still pass the filter, so the empty-result BAD_REQUEST on line 80 still fires only when nothing valid remains.
The result must still be an array of guest email strings consumable by the later `uniqueGuests.map`. Keeping the original casing or storing a lowercased form are both acceptable.
items.notes: The blacklist side is already lowercased on line 71, so a fix only needs to lowercase the guest for that check.
