For the attendee check, it must normalize both the guest and attendee.email. Valid approaches include toLowerCase on both sides or a precomputed lowercased Set. Trimming whitespace from blacklist entries is a nice extra but not required. Deduplicating repeated guests within the input itself (e.g. `a@x.com` and `A@x.com` in the same request) is also beyond the finding and optional. Do not penalize a fix that leaves line 71 unchanged.

items.defectStatement: In useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, when `rule` is undefined (the skipToken path), useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable returns loading=false. MaybeSupported therefore becomes AlwaysSupported, and Duplicate resolves to `toAbility(AlwaysSupported, grafana create)`. Callers that OR this result with the ruler-based ability (e.g. for data-source rules) then report Duplicate as allowed whenever the user has Grafana rule-create permission, even when the ruler path denies it.
obligations: When `rule` is undefined, Duplicate must not be reported as supported or allowed, whatever the user's Grafana create permission is.
When `rule` is undefined, the other support-gated abilities (Update, Delete, Pause, Restore, DeletePermanently) must also not be reported as supported.

For a defined rule, existing behavior must be preserved: not supported while loading, supported once loaded, Duplicate not supported for plugin-provided rules, and Update/Delete-style abilities not supported for immutable rules.
Duplicate must still be gated by the Grafana rules create permission.
items.notes: Valid fixes include `!rule || loading ? NotSupported : AlwaysSupported`, an early return of all-NotSupported abilities when the rule is undefined, or an equivalent guard applied to duplicateSupported and MaybeSupported. If a fix also references `rule` in the memo, the dependency array must still include it (it already does). View and Explore use AlwaysSupported independently of the rule; leaving them unchanged is acceptable because the finding's main concern is Duplicate leaking through the OR in AlertRuleMenu. The AlertRuleMenu OR is outside the shown code, so the caller impact is plausible but cannot be verified here. The undefined-rule MaybeSupported result is a real defect regardless.

items.defectStatement: Lines 553-567 pass an async callback to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach`, so every promise from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` and `deleteMeeting` is discarded. The reschedule-request email and BOOKING_CANCELLED webhooks then run before the calendar/video deletions finish, and any rejection from a deletion is never observed (an unhandled promise rejection).
obligations: All calendar/video deletion promises must be collected and awaited (e.g. `await Promise.all`/`Promise.allSettled` over a `map`, or a sequential `for...of` with `await`) before execution reaches `sendRequestRescheduleEmail` at line 570.
Rejections from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` must be observed (awaited and caught/logged or deliberately propagated), not left as unhandled rejections.

Per-reference logic must stay the same: skip refs without `uid`; for `_calendar` types, resolve the calendar from `credentialsMap` and call `deleteEvent(uid, builder.calendarEvent, externalCalendarId)` with optional chaining for a null calendar; for `_video` types, call `deleteMeeting(credential, uid)`; ignore other types.
items.notes: No try/catch around the forEach appears in the shown window, so that part of the finding is unverified or overstated. The core defect still stands. The diff introduced the async callback when `getCalendar` became async, but `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` promises were already discarded before the change. Plain `Promise.all` is acceptable but changes behavior: one failed deletion would reject the mutation and skip the email/webhooks. `Promise.allSettled` or per-item `.catch` with logging preserves the previous non-blocking behavior, and a grader may prefer it. Either approach satisfies the awaiting requirement. Sequential `for...of` is also valid. A fix that merely wraps `forEach` in try/catch does not fix the defect.

items.defectStatement: In CleanUpService.Run the ticker interval was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, so every cleanup job (tmp files, snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history) now runs 10x as often. That multiplies DB and filesystem load. It also conflicts with clean()'s 9-minute timeout, which was sized for a 10-minute cadence: a slow run can last far longer than one tick interval, so runs end up back-to-back.
obligations: The periodic cadence for the full set of cleanup jobs must no longer be 1 minute; restore 10 minutes or an equivalent non-aggressive interval consistent with the 9-minute job timeout.
Preserve the initial cleanUpTmpFiles call before the loop and the select loop that runs srv.clean on each tick and returns ctx.Err() on ctx.Done().
If a faster cadence is kept for any job (e.g., annotations), it must apply only to that job, not to all cleanup jobs.
items.notes: Simplest valid fix: revert to time.Minute * 10. A config-driven interval, or a separate faster ticker limited to annotation cleanup, is also acceptable. Any separate ticker must stay within the cited Run lines. Adding ticker.Stop() via defer is a fine optional improvement but not required.

items.defectStatement: The diff moved `cacheMu` from guarding all of `BuildIndex` to guarding only `b.cache[key] = idx` (lines 137-139). Concurrent `BuildIndex` calls for the same `NamespacedResource` now run index creation, builder and Flush in parallel. Same-key file builds race on the same directory (`Root/Namespace/<Resource>.<Group>`), duplicate the builder work and increment `IndexTenants` once per build. Whichever build finishes last overwrites the cache entry, and the losing index is left open.
obligations: Concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key must not both create/build an index; per-key (or global) mutual exclusion must cover creation through the cache write.
The cache map write must still happen under cacheMu, and a successful build must still store the index in b.cache and return it.
Builds for different keys should not be needlessly serialized if a per-key scheme is used; a single global lock restoring the old behavior is also acceptable.
Error paths must still return (nil, err) without caching, and no lock may be left held on any return path.
items.notes: Real mutual exclusion requires acquiring the lock or singleflight before index creation (around lines 94-98), which lies outside the cited lines 137-140. A fix that only edits the cache write, e.g. check-and-return-existing, prevents clobbering but not duplicate work; treat it as partial. Valid fixes: restore the function-wide `cacheMu` lock (the original behavior), a per-key mutex map, or `singleflight` keyed by NamespacedResource. Overstatement: `bleve.New` on an already-existing path returns an error, so the second same-key file build likely fails rather than silently contending. `IndexTenants` is still incremented even on that error path. The unlocked read of `b.cache` in `TotalDocs` is a separate issue, not required here.

items.defectStatement: In DualWriterMode3.Create's async goroutine (lines 55-56), the error returned by d.Legacy.Create (errObjectSt) is only reduced to a boolean for recordLegacyDuration and never logged. Before this PR, a legacy create failure was logged ('unable to create object in legacy storage'), so legacy write failures and drift are now invisible except as a metric count.
obligations: When d.Legacy.Create returns a non-nil error, that error must be logged at error level. Use the request's contextual logger (the `log` built with kind/method values, or klog.FromContext(ctx)) and include a message identifying a legacy-storage create failure.
No error log is emitted when the legacy create succeeds.

Preserve the existing behavior: the legacy create stays asynchronous with the 10s timeout context, recordLegacyDuration is still called with errObjectSt != nil and the same arguments, and the function's return value is unaffected.
items.notes: The fix only covers the cited lines in Create. The same omission exists in the Delete, Update and DeleteCollection goroutines, but those are outside the cited range and should not be required. Both captured `log` and klog.FromContext(ctx) are acceptable, since ctx carries `log` via klog.NewContext. Adding the object (e.g. created) as a log value is optional. Logging must happen inside the goroutine. Unrelated issues in the file are out of scope: DeleteCollection's goroutine calls recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, and the storage-failure path calls recordLegacyDuration.

items.defectStatement: In DualWriterMode3.Delete, line 106 records the successful storage-delete duration with `name` (the object name) as the kind label instead of `options.Kind`. Successful delete metrics are therefore labeled by object name rather than kind, which is inconsistent with the error path (line 103) and every other method, and creates one metric series per deleted object name.
obligations: The success-path recordStorageDuration call on line 106 must use `options.Kind` (the same kind value used at line 103 and elsewhere) as the kind label, not `name`.
Preserve the other arguments: isError=false, mode3Str, method ("delete"), and startStorage timing.
It must still call recordStorageDuration, not recordLegacyDuration, since this measures the Storage delete.
items.notes: This is a one-token fix. Nearby issues are out of scope for the cited line and must not be required: line 97 passes d.Log instead of log to the context, Create and Update error paths call recordLegacyDuration, and the DeleteCollection goroutine calls recordStorageDuration. A fix that rewrites other lines is outside the cited range.

items.defectStatement: In test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling, the final assertion expects that no offset is committed for test_partition after offset 100 fails. That is the opposite of the real behavior. The worker marks offsets complete even on failure, so the commit loop eventually commits 102 (next offset after 101). The test passes only because it checks about 0.2s after processing, before the roughly once-per-second commit tick, so it is timing-dependent and verifies nothing meaningful.
obligations: The wait loop must wait (bounded) until a commit for test_partition is observed, rather than breaking right after processing finishes plus a short sleep.
The assertions must check that test_partition is in committed_offsets and that its committed value is 102. This shows the failed message at 100 did not block committing past it.
Keep the existing check that mock_processor_call.call_count == 2, and keep the bounded wait so the test cannot hang.
The wait budget must exceed the commit interval (more than about 1s; for example the existing 20×0.1s or longer) so the test is not flaky.
items.notes: Valid variants include: extending the existing loop's condition to also require test_partition in committed_offsets, or adding a separate polling loop. Asserting 101 is wrong, because the commit offset is the next offset to read. Keeping the 'no commit' assertion, or only lengthening the sleep, does not fix the defect. The test docstring already says errors shouldn't block commits, which matches the fix.

items.defectStatement: In `join()`, once the timeout deadline has passed, the `break` at line 341 exits the loop. Every process not yet visited is then neither waited on nor `terminate()`d, so it is leaked until interpreter exit. The old single-process code always reached `terminate()` after waiting; the new loop only terminates processes visited before the deadline expired.
obligations: After the deadline expires, every remaining process in `self.processes` must still reach the termination step instead of being skipped.

Waiting must still respect the overall deadline: no extra blocking per process after the deadline, and no waiting at all after it has expired. With no timeout, the code must keep waiting until each process is no longer alive.
Thread entries (the `produce_to_pipe` path) must not have `terminate()` called on them; keep the type guard or an equivalent check.
items.notes: Valid fixes include skipping only the wait (not the terminate) once the deadline has passed, or terminating all processes in a separate loop after the wait loop. Possible trap: `mp_context.Process` produces `SpawnProcess`, and `isinstance(SpawnProcess(), multiprocessing.Process)` may be False. If so, `terminate()` never actually runs, and the old code had the same issue. A fix that also broadens the guard (e.g. to `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` or a `hasattr` check) is acceptable but not required. The finding's core claim about the `break` is accurate.

items.defectStatement: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() and terminate() call self.queue_pool.shutdown() on a FixedQueuePool that the strategy does not own; it is injected and, per the finding, shared by the factory across strategies. After a rebalance, the old strategy's close shuts down every queue and joins the workers. The next strategy's queue_pool.submit then raises queue.ShutDown, and submit()'s except branch marks those offsets complete, so messages get committed without being processed.
obligations: close() and terminate() must not shut down or otherwise disable the injected queue pool; it must stay usable by a strategy created later from the same factory.
close() must still stop this strategy's commit thread: set shutdown_event and join the thread with a bounded timeout.
terminate() must still signal this strategy's commit thread to stop, and must not block indefinitely.

The pool must still be shut down somewhere, for example in the factory's shutdown. Simply deleting the call with no owner left to shut it down is only acceptable if the grader accepts that the owner handles it outside the cited lines.
items.notes: The factory is not shown, so the shared-pool premise comes from the finding; the strategy does receive the pool by injection, which is consistent with that. The harm is somewhat mis-stated: offsets do not 'leak'. queue.ShutDown from put is caught in submit and the offset is marked complete, so the real effect is silent message loss with the offset committed. The 'multiple commit threads' part is mostly overstated, because arroyo closes the old strategy, which joins its commit thread, before creating a new one; only terminate() lacks a join, and that is minor. Accept these as valid fixes: removing the pool shutdown from the strategy (the owner shuts it down instead), or an ownership flag or reference count so that only the last or owning strategy shuts it down. An optional final commit before stopping is fine but not required. A fix that recreates the pool inside close is wrong.

items.defectStatement: In `submit()`, a `FilteredPayload` message is passed straight to `self.decoder`; any failure is logged as an error, and nothing explicitly handles filtered messages. The finding's core claim is wrong, though: `FilteredPayload` is the payload type, not the value type. Such messages still arrive as `BrokerValue`, so either the `result is None` path or the except handler already adds and completes their offset; they are not silently skipped.
obligations: A message whose `message.payload` is a `FilteredPayload` (with `message.value` a `BrokerValue`) must have its partition/offset added and completed in `offset_tracker`, so commits can advance past it.
Filtered messages must not be enqueued to `queue_pool` or passed to `grouping_fn`, and should not produce an error/exception log.
Non-filtered message behavior must be preserved: decode, mark offset done immediately when the result is None, otherwise build a `WorkItem` and call `queue_pool.submit`.
The except handler must still add and complete the offset for `BrokerValue` messages on any failure.
items.notes: The finding conflates payload type with value type: the `isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue)` check is about the value wrapper, so filtered messages from the broker do pass it. Treat the finding as overstated. A fix that checks `isinstance(message.payload, FilteredPayload)` up front and marks the offset done is acceptable but not strictly required. Keeping the decoder handling `FilteredPayload` by returning None is also acceptable, since that path already tracks offsets. Do not accept fixes that check `message.value` for `FilteredPayload`; that is wrong. Do not accept fixes that drop offset tracking for filtered messages.

items.defectStatement: In gen_request_data (lines 153-155), the error's `timestamp`, which comes from nodestore event data as float seconds, is compared directly against the rrweb event `timestamp`, which is in milliseconds. Every error therefore compares as earlier than the first replay event and is emitted ahead of all breadcrumbs, so the interleaved chronological order sent to Seer is wrong.
obligations: The comparison must put the error timestamp and the rrweb event timestamp in the same unit, for example error seconds*1000 vs event ms, or event ms/1000 vs error seconds, before deciding whether to emit the error.
An error must be emitted before an event only when it actually occurred earlier in time, and the strict `<` ordering semantics must be preserved.
The loop structure, error_idx advancement, bounds check, and the `event.get("timestamp", 0)` fallback for events without a timestamp must be preserved.
The stored error timestamp values must not be mutated in a way that changes the text produced by generate_error_log_message, unless that change is done deliberately and consistently.
items.notes: Converting either side is a valid fix. Normalizing at fetch time in fetch_error_details is outside the cited lines and would also change the timestamp shown in the log message. The finding is accurate. Errors with a missing timestamp default to 0.0, which is still earliest after conversion; that is acceptable.

items.defectStatement: Each worker queue in `FixedQueuePool.__init__` is created as an unbounded `queue.Queue()`, and `FixedQueuePool.submit` enqueues without any depth check. If the Kafka consumer submits faster than the per-queue worker threads drain, queued `WorkItem`s (each holding the full message) and tracked offsets grow without limit, risking OOM. This also contradicts the strategy docstring's claim of "natural backpressure when queues fill up."
obligations: Each per-group queue must have a finite capacity, either via a maxsize or an explicit depth check in submit, so the backlog cannot grow unboundedly.
When a queue is full, submit must not silently drop the item. It must either block or signal backpressure (e.g. by raising), so the caller can retry the same message.

Offset bookkeeping must stay consistent: an offset must not be left in `offset_tracker` as outstanding unless the item was actually enqueued. Otherwise commits stall permanently. Either check capacity before `add_offset`, or undo it on failure.
Preserve consistent group-to-queue hashing, FIFO order per queue, one worker per queue, and normal behavior when queues are not full.
items.notes: Several fixes are valid: bounded `Queue(maxsize=N)` with a blocking `put` (optionally with a timeout), or a non-blocking check that raises arroyo's `MessageRejected` / `queue.Full`. In arroyo, raising `MessageRejected` is the idiomatic form of backpressure. An indefinite blocking `put` can stall the consumer thread past `max.poll.interval` and trigger a rebalance; that is acceptable but less ideal. Making the limit configurable is a plus, not a requirement. Trap: the caller `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit` (outside the cited lines) catches all Exceptions and marks the offset complete. A raised `MessageRejected` or `Full` would therefore be swallowed and the message skipped. Do not fail a fix for this, since it lies outside the cited lines, but note it. Fail a fix that calls `add_offset` and then a non-blocking put that raises, without rolling the offset back.

items.defectStatement: `_commit_loop` runs on a background daemon thread and calls Arroyo's `commit_function` there. That callback touches StreamProcessor and Kafka consumer state, which is not thread-safe, so it races with the main thread's `poll`/`_run_once`. The loop can also commit after shutdown or partition revocation: when `shutdown_event` fires during `wait(1.0)`, the loop still runs one more iteration body and commits.
obligations: `commit_function` must no longer be called from the background thread. Any commit must happen on the processor's main thread (e.g. from `poll`/`submit`/`close`), or be otherwise serialized so it cannot run concurrently with the main thread or after the strategy is closed.
No commit may happen after `shutdown_event` is set. The iteration that wakes because of shutdown must not commit from the background thread.
Offsets must be passed to `mark_committed` only for offsets actually handed to `commit_function`, never before or without the commit. Otherwise those offsets are silently skipped and never committed.
Contiguous-offset semantics from `get_committable_offsets`, the per-partition `committed` metric, and exception logging in the loop must be preserved.
items.notes: The fix is limited to lines 273-291, but a proper main-thread handoff also needs `poll()` (and ideally `close`) to drain the pending offsets and commit them. Accept a loop that only computes or stashes committable offsets (thread-safely, merging with or overwriting the previous pending set) without committing, provided it is clear the main thread performs the commit. Removing the thread entirely and computing offsets in `poll` is also valid. A lock taken only inside `_commit_loop` does NOT fix the race, because the main thread never acquires it; only accept the lock approach if the lock is clearly shared with the main-thread paths. Wrapping the existing call in an `if not shutdown_event.is_set()` check alone still leaves the cross-thread race.

items.defectStatement: The react-query key at lines 39-42 is ['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions]. It contains no organization identifier, while the fetcher from useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys calls the org-scoped endpoint. If the user switches organizations with the same traceItemType, type, datetime and project IDs, the cache entry for the previous org is reused. That shows the wrong org's attribute keys until a refetch happens.
obligations: The queryKey must include an organization-distinguishing value (e.g. organization.slug or id), so keys for different orgs with otherwise identical options differ.
Keep the existing key components: the 'use-trace-item-attribute-keys' prefix and queryOptions (traceItemType, type, datetime, projectIds), so other parameter changes still produce distinct keys.
Keep the key memoized, with dependencies that include the org value, so it is recomputed when the org changes.
Hooks must stay valid: useOrganization() (or similar) must be called at the top level of the hook, not inside useMemo.
items.notes: A complete fix likely needs an import or a hook call outside the cited lines, e.g. importing useOrganization and calling it at the top of the hook. Accept that. Equally valid: getting the org from an existing context value, or putting the org into queryOptions upstream. The internals of makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions are not shown; if it already embedded the org, the finding would be moot, but nothing visible here suggests it does. Separately, environment no longer seems to be in the key (the old code passed selection.environments). That is a related but distinct issue and not required for this finding.

items.defectStatement: Both `zunionstore` calls (lines 47 and 53) omit `AGGREGATE`, so Redis uses the default SUM. A payload present in both `set_key` and the merged set (`span_key` or `parent_key`) ends up scored with the sum of its two scores instead of a single timestamp-like score. That inflated score sorts it as the newest member, so the `zpopmin` cap at line 63 evicts other spans first and oldest-first eviction breaks.
obligations: Both `zunionstore` calls must merge duplicate members to a score taken from one of the inputs (e.g. `AGGREGATE MAX` or `AGGREGATE MIN`) rather than summing them.
The `AGGREGATE` option must be valid ZUNIONSTORE syntax: placed after the two source keys, with numkeys still 2 and the destination and sources unchanged.
Keep assigning the `zunionstore` result to `span_count` and keep the following `unlink` of the merged key in each branch.
Keep the existing branch conditions unchanged: `not is_root_span` with a non-empty `span_key`, and `set_span_id ~= parent_span_id` with a non-empty `parent_key`.
items.notes: MAX and MIN are both acceptable; MAX keeps the latest timestamp. Fixing only one of the two calls is incomplete. The ZADD that sets scores is not shown; the assumption that scores are end timestamps comes from the finding. The bug only shows up when the same payload is in both sets (duplicates or redeliveries), but it is real. Passing explicit WEIGHTS is unnecessary; the change is just the AGGREGATE option.

items.defectStatement: The trim at lines 62-64 pops the lowest-scored members (earliest end_timestamp_precise) from the segment set with no exemption for the segment's own span, the member whose span_id equals set_span_id. A remote segment span, or a root whose end timestamp is skewed earlier than its children's, can be evicted once the set exceeds 1000 members. The segment is then flushed without its root, while the has_root_span flag still says it has one.
obligations: When span_count > 1000, the member whose decoded span_id equals set_span_id must not be removed, even if it has one of the lowest scores; it must stay in set_key with its original score.

The other evicted members must still be the lowest-scored non-segment spans, and the set must stay capped at about 1000 members (exactly 1000 including the root, or 1000 plus the root, are both acceptable).
When span_count <= 1000, behavior must be unchanged (no removals), and the script must not error when the segment span is absent from the set or a member cannot be decoded.
items.notes: Members are opaque payload strings, so identifying the root means decoding them with cjson (available in Redis Lua) and comparing span_id to set_span_id. Several approaches are valid: pop and then re-ZADD the root with its score; ZRANGE the victim range and ZREM all but the root, adjusting the count; or skip the root and evict one more. Do not require the finding's exact ZRANGEBYSCORE recipe. Root eviction is uncommon because a root usually ends last, but the clock-skew and remote-segment cases are real. A fix that relies on is_root_span alone is wrong: that flag describes the current incoming span, not the set's root member.

items.defectStatement: Lines 17-18 make `.d-header .contents` a flex container. Its children, including the header-extra-info component's outer Ember wrapper div, become flex items with the default `min-width: auto`. The `overflow: hidden` / ellipsis rule lives on the inner `.extra-info-wrapper`, not on that flex item. With a long, non-wrapping topic title the outer item cannot shrink below its content width, so the title ellipsis stops working and the `.panel` (order 3, `margin-left: auto`) is pushed out of or overflows the header.
obligations: When the topic title is long and non-wrapping, the flex item that contains the extra-info/title must be able to shrink below its content width. This can be done with `min-width: 0` or `overflow: hidden` on the actual flex child, or by putting the constrained wrapper class directly on that element.
The title must still truncate with an ellipsis, and `.panel` must stay inside the header and stay right-aligned.
Keep the flex layout of `.contents`: `display: flex` plus vertical centering with `align-items: center`, including the vendor-prefixed mixins.
Other header children (logo/home icon, panel) must not be shrunk or clipped unintentionally.
items.notes: Several fixes are valid. Examples: add a rule inside `.contents` such as `> * { min-width: 0 }` or `> .ember-view { min-width: 0 }`, or a selector that targets the component's outer element. Moving the class onto the component element via `classNames` is also valid but happens outside these lines. A fix limited to lines 17-18 must still do something that reaches the flex child. Removing flexbox altogether is not an acceptable fix, because it undoes the intended refactor. The component markup is not shown, so the claim about the Ember outer div is plausible but unverified. Grade on whether the actual flex child can shrink.

items.defectStatement: `include_website_name` (lines 153-155) lacks the trailing `?`, so ActiveModel::Serializers never calls it and `website_name` is always serialized. `website_name` is also not in `untrusted_attributes`, so it is exposed even when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true. This leaks the host/path of the website that `website` itself correctly hides.
obligations: The cited method must be a real AMS include hook named `include_website_name?`, so it actually controls inclusion of `website_name`.
`website_name` must be excluded whenever `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true, even if a website is set.
When fields are not restricted, `website_name` must still be included only if `website.present?`.
Other attributes and the existing `untrusted_attributes` behavior for `website` and the rest must stay unchanged.
items.notes: Adding :website_name to `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111) is a valid alternative, but those lines are outside the cited range. Trap: `untrusted_attributes` generates `include_<attr>?` methods. A hand-written `include_website_name?` at line 153 is defined later in the class body and would override any generated one. So a fix in the cited lines that only renames the method and keeps `website.present?` still leaks. It must check `!scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` itself. Accept either order of the two conditions, and safe navigation if used.

items.defectStatement: The redirect-resolution loop (line 30) now stops after 1001 hops instead of the previous 10001. When a redirect chain in `span-buf:sr` is deeper than that, `set_span_id` resolves to an intermediate span rather than the real segment root. The span is then recorded and merged into the wrong set, which splits the segment. The reduction appears tied to the new 1000-span eviction cap, but the two limits are unrelated.
obligations: The redirect-chasing loop must allow traversal depth of at least 10000 hops (the prior behavior), or otherwise not be bounded by the 1000-span eviction cap.
The loop semantics must be preserved: break when there is no redirect or on a self-redirect, follow `new_set_span` otherwise, and record `redirect_depth = i` for the returned value.
The variables `set_span_id` (initialized to `parent_span_id`) and `redirect_depth` (initialized to 0) must keep their current meaning for the downstream code at lines 40-72.
items.notes: Restoring `0, 10000`, optionally with the original explanatory comment, is the expected fix. Defining a separate named max-depth constant is also valid. The 1000-span eviction cap (`zpopmin`, lines 62-63) lies outside the cited lines and must not be changed or merged with the traversal limit. The finding's claim that the change has "no functional need" is a judgment call, since a lower limit bounds Lua runtime. However, the change silently regresses correctness for deep chains, so the finding is valid. An unbounded loop is a questionable fix because a redirect cycle longer than one hop could hang Redis.

items.defectStatement: In remove_member (line 90), `group.users.delete(user_id)` drops the membership row but never clears the removed user's `primary_group_id`. A user whose primary group was this group keeps its flair and title after leaving it. The previous removal path (`group.remove` / `usernames=` → `destroy_deletions`) nulled it.
obligations: After removing the membership, the removed user's primary_group_id must be set to nil if, and only if, it equals this group's id.
Other users, and a removed user whose primary group is a different group, must keep their primary_group_id unchanged.
The membership must still be removed, and the existing automatic-group guard and success/error JSON responses must stay as they are.
items.notes: The finding's `User.where(id: user_id, primary_group_id: group.id).update_all(primary_group_id: nil)` is one valid fix. Equivalents are also fine: load the user and clear the field conditionally, or call a model method such as `group.remove(user)` if it demonstrably resets primary_group_id. The `destroy_deletions` behavior lives in the Group model and is not visible in the shown code. Reject an unconditional reset of primary_group_id, since that would wipe a different primary group. Reset ordering relative to group.save is not critical.

items.defectStatement: Fallback locales are preloaded only by the `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` call in `ApplicationController#set_locale` (line 159), so only web requests get them. Code that switches locale outside a request (background jobs via `I18n.locale=`, `PostAlerter`/mailers via `I18n.with_locale(user.effective_locale)`) can resolve a fallback chain to locales that were never loaded. Those translations then come back missing instead of falling back.
obligations: Fallback locales for the active locale must be loaded before translation in non-request contexts (jobs, mailers, `with_locale` blocks), not only in the controller `set_locale` path.
The existing web-request behavior must be preserved: after `set_locale` runs, the fallback locales for the user's effective locale (or the site default) are loaded.
The fix must not load all locales eagerly on every call or repeatedly reload locales that are already loaded; loading should stay idempotent.
items.notes: The replacement covers only line 159, so a fix there cannot reach the job or mailer paths by itself. Acceptable approaches include: moving the ensure-loaded logic into a shared hook that runs on every locale change (for example overriding `I18n.locale=`/`with_locale`, or making the fallback lookup or backend load fallback locales lazily on first use), or calling it explicitly in `Jobs::Base`/`PostAlerter`. A fix at line 159 is valid only if it delegates to such a global, lazy mechanism. Removing the call without a replacement is wrong. The surrounding code is not visible, so the claim about missing loads in jobs is plausible but not verified here.

items.defectStatement: In the public group members route, setupController calls `model.findMembers()` with no offset or limit. It therefore loads only the first page (default limit 50), and the public members template has no pagination or load-more control, so members past the first page of a group are never shown. Before this change the route loaded all members for non-automatic groups.
obligations: The public group members view must be able to show every member of a group with more members than the default page size, either by loading all of them or by making further pages reachable.
Keep setting `showing` to 'members' on the group controller and keep the group model as the controller's model.
Keep loading members when the route is entered, so the first page still appears without extra user action.
items.notes: Several fixes are valid within the cited lines: request a large or unlimited limit, or loop and fetch pages until `user_count` is reached. A load-more action is also valid, but it needs template or controller changes outside the cited lines, so the in-scope fix is most likely loading all members. The call is not awaited, so the page renders before the data arrives; that is not the defect being graded. Exact `findMembers` signature and parameters are not shown, so do not penalize reasonable assumptions about how offset and limit are passed.

items.defectStatement: Line 48 fetches the attacker-influenced embed URL with open-uri's `open(url).read`. The only upstream check, TopicRetriever#invalid_host?, compares just the hostname, so the server can be made to request arbitrary ports or paths on that host, and open-uri follows redirects to internal or private addresses (SSRF). `Kernel#open` on a raw string can also open local files or pipe commands if a non-URI string ever reaches it.
obligations: The fetch must not use bare `Kernel#open`/open-uri on the raw string. It must parse the URL and reject any scheme other than http or https before any network or file access.
Redirects must not be followed blindly. Either disable them, or re-validate each redirect target (scheme, host and port, and that it does not resolve to a private, loopback or link-local address).

The fetch must be hardened against internal targets: restrict the port to 80/443 or the embeddable host's expected port, and/or refuse destinations resolving to private, loopback or link-local IPs. It must include a bounded timeout.

On success, the fetched HTML body must still be passed to `Readability::Document.new` with the same tags/attributes options on lines 49-50, and the statement must stay syntactically valid. On rejection or failure it must fail safely (raise or return without importing) instead of fetching.
items.notes: Valid implementations include Net::HTTP or FinalDestination-style logic, Excon/Faraday with redirects off, or `URI.parse(url).open(redirect: false, ...)` plus an IP check. A helper method defined elsewhere is acceptable if the cited line calls it. Doing the scheme/port/IP validation in TopicRetriever#invalid_host? alone does not fix this line, and it would still leave redirects exploitable. A fix that only switches to `URI.parse(url).open` (still following redirects, no IP or port checks) is insufficient. The command-execution angle is mitigated upstream by the host check, since a nil host fails it, but avoiding `Kernel#open` is still required.

items.defectStatement: Lines 9-16 index row 0 of both `execute` results without checking that any row came back. If no `embed_category` setting matches a category name, or `uncategorized_category_id` is absent, `[0]` on the empty PG::Result raises an exception and aborts the migration.
obligations: Before reading row 0 of the embed_category lookup, check that the result has at least one row. When it is empty, fall through to the uncategorized fallback instead of raising.
Guard the uncategorized_category_id lookup the same way, so an empty result does not raise.
When both lookups find nothing, `category_id` must end up as a defined integer so the later INSERTs and the DELETE still run.
When rows exist, the result must not change: use the embed_category's id if it is non-zero, otherwise use uncategorized_category_id as an integer.
items.notes: The finding says NoMethodError on nil. With the pg gem, `PG::Result#[]` on an out-of-range index typically raises IndexError instead. Either way the migration crashes, so the defect stands. Any of these guards is acceptable: checking `cmd_tuples`/`ntuples > 0` (the same style line 19 uses), `to_a.first`/`first` with safe navigation, or a rescue. The default when nothing is found is up to the fix; 0 matches the existing `.to_i` semantics. Do not require changes outside lines 9-16, such as the SQL injection risk in the line 25 INSERT.

items.defectStatement: Line 35 calls `i.content.scrub` unconditionally, but SimpleRSS leaves `content` nil for items without that tag, such as RSS 2.0 items that only have `<description>`. The resulting NoMethodError aborts the whole feed loop, and since the job has `retry: false`, no later items are imported in that run.
obligations: Must not raise when `i.content` is nil. Use a fallback body, at least `i.description`, when content is absent.
Items with no usable body (all candidates nil or blank) must be skipped, e.g. with `next`, rather than raising or passing a nil body to TopicEmbed.import; the remaining items must still be processed.
When a body is present, keep the existing `scrub` plus `CGI.unescapeHTML` treatment, and keep the result in the `content` variable that line 36 uses.
items.notes: In SimpleRSS, `content:encoded` is likely exposed as `content_encoded` rather than `content`. If so, the finding's claim that `content` is set for content:encoded is probably inaccurate. A fix that also falls back to `i.content_encoded` and/or `i.summary` is acceptable and arguably better, but it is not required as long as `description` is a fallback. The TopicRetriever synchronous call is not visible here, so do not grade on it. Any equivalent nil-safe pattern is fine (`||` chain, `.presence`, safe navigation), provided blank bodies are skipped and the scrub/unescape is not applied to nil.

items.defectStatement: In `unsubscribe`, `TopicUser.find_by` (line 105) returns nil when the user has no TopicUser row for the topic, such as someone emailed about a topic they never opened. Line 107 then calls `tu.notification_level` on nil and raises NoMethodError, so the unsubscribe link 500s.
obligations: When no TopicUser row exists for (current_user, topic_id), the action must not raise. Execution must reach lines 108-113 with a non-nil `tu` that can be saved with `save!`, for example via find_or_initialize_by, find_or_create_by, or an explicit create.

The comparison on line 107 must not operate on a nil `notification_level`. A newly built record must have a usable level, either from the column default or set explicitly, so a user with no prior record ends up muted or regular rather than erroring.
Existing behavior for users who already have a record must be preserved. A level above regular is lowered to regular; otherwise the level becomes muted. The same user_id/topic_id lookup must be kept.
items.notes: Only lines 105-107 are replaced, and lines 108-113 still dereference `tu`. A fix that merely guards the comparison (e.g. `tu&.notification_level` or `if tu && ...`) without supplying a record still crashes at line 110 or 113 and is incorrect. The finding's suggestion of `TopicUser.get` is a trap: in Discourse it is essentially a find_by wrapper and can also return nil, so it does not fix the bug by itself. find_or_create_by, find_or_initialize_by, or create-on-nil are all acceptable. A minor race on the unique index is not required to be handled.

items.defectStatement: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with only `pass`, so the base class's abstract methods are never implemented. Instantiating the handler (e.g. via Detector.detector_handler for a MetricAlertFire-typed detector) therefore raises TypeError, whereas the previous DetectorHandler subclass with a stub evaluate() could be instantiated.
obligations: MetricAlertDetectorHandler must be instantiable: no abstract methods may remain on the class, whichever base it uses.

If it stays a StatefulDetectorHandler subclass, it must override every abstract method of that base (e.g. counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data) with signatures compatible with the base, so that type checking and runtime both work.
Stub implementations must not raise on normal calls. Returning empty or neutral values is acceptable, consistent with the prior no-op evaluate() that returned [].
The class must remain generic over QuerySubscriptionUpdate and remain usable as MetricAlertFire.detector_handler.
items.notes: The exact set of abstract methods depends on StatefulDetectorHandler, which is not shown; the four names in the finding are plausible but unverified. Accept either fix: reverting to a DetectorHandler subclass with a stub evaluate() returning [] (this also requires restoring the DataPacket and DetectorEvaluationResult imports, which fall outside the cited lines), or implementing the abstract overrides. A fix that only adds some of the overrides is incorrect.

items.defectStatement: Lines 63-70 downsize the image by overwriting `tempfile.path` while the Tempfile is still open, and the loop guard reads `tempfile.size` from that open handle. If the resize tool writes a new file and renames it over the path (a new inode), the handle still points at the original file. The loop then sees the old size, and `Upload.create_for` on line 72 gets the old size and content, so the downsizing has no effect.
obligations: After each downsize, the loop guard must check the size of the downsized file now at the path, not a stale handle.

When the block ends, the `tempfile` object used on line 72 must report the new size and read the new content from the start. That means reopening or rewinding it, or replacing it with a handle that is still cleaned up. Fixing only the loop check, e.g. with `File.size(path)`, leaves line 72 stale.
Keep the existing behaviour: the entry conditions (tempfile present, non-empty, `max_image_size_kb` > 0, is an image), at most 5 attempts at 80%, and the `allow_animation` option.
The temporary file must still be closed and unlinked by the `ensure` block's `tempfile.try(:close!)`. Do not swap in a plain File, which has no `close!` and would leak the temp file.
items.notes: The finding is plausible but conditional. Ruby's `Tempfile#size` flushes and fstats the open descriptor. If ImageMagick truncates and rewrites the same inode, which is common, the size is already correct. The real risk is the rename-into-place case, plus buffered or stale read state. Valid fixes include: calling `tempfile.open` or `reopen(path)` plus `rewind` after downsizing, or downsizing to a separate temp path and copying the bytes back into the open tempfile. A grader should reject fixes that only change the loop condition, because line 72 is outside the cited range and still uses `tempfile` and `tempfile.size`.

items.defectStatement: In get_committable_offsets (lines 86-96), the scan walks every integer from start to max_offset and stops at the first one missing from all_offsets. Kafka offsets can have gaps (transaction markers, compaction), so each call stops at the first gap even when every later delivered offset is already completed. The gap is only skipped on the next 1-second cycle, after mark_committed has trimmed all_offsets and moved min_offset past it, so commits advance at most one gap per cycle and lag can grow on gappy partitions.
obligations: Offsets that were never delivered (missing from all_offsets) must not stop the commit from advancing in the same call. The result must be the highest tracked offset above last_committed such that no tracked offset at or below it is still outstanding.
Never return an offset at or beyond any still-outstanding tracked offset for that partition. The scan must still stop at the first outstanding tracked offset in ascending order.

Preserve the existing output contract: include a partition only when the computed offset is greater than last_committed, and return the raw processed offset with the same semantics as now (no +1 change).
items.notes: The finding says the partition 'never commits again'; that is overstated. Because mark_committed trims all_offsets and start uses min_offset, a gap is skipped one cycle later. The real impact is throttled progress, not a permanent stall. A minimal valid fix within the cited lines is to iterate over sorted tracked offsets at or above start, rather than over range(start, max_offset+1), and break on the first outstanding one. The finding's per-partition deque is a valid alternative but is not required. Do not penalize fixes that keep the set-based structures. Do penalize fixes that skip past outstanding offsets or that commit untracked offsets beyond the highest tracked one.

items.defectStatement: When the `use-table-widget-visualization` flag is on, `tableResultComponent` (lines 164-174) renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and a hard-coded empty `tableData` (`data: []`, empty `fields`/`units` meta). It ignores `result.data`, `result.meta` and `widget.queries[i]` fields, so every table widget shows no rows or columns for flagged orgs.
obligations: The flagged branch must pass the per-result data (`result.data`) to `TableWidgetVisualization`, not a hard-coded empty array.

Meta passed to `TableWidgetVisualization` must come from `result.meta` (field types and units), not empty objects. It must be adapted to the `{fields, units}` shape the component expects, and must tolerate missing or undefined meta.
Columns must come from the widget query's fields (`widget.queries[i]` fields/aliases, or the computed `fields`/`fieldAliases`), so the rendered columns match the query's columns.
The non-flagged `StyledSimpleTableChart` branch and the per-result mapping/key behavior must stay unchanged.
items.notes: This looks like a placeholder or WIP scaffold behind a feature flag. Still, the shipped behavior is an empty table for flagged orgs, so the finding is valid. Several shapes are acceptable: inline mapping, or a helper or converter that turns discover meta and fields into the `TableWidgetVisualization` columns/tableData format. Exact column prop shape (e.g. `{key, name/alias, type}`) depends on the component API, so don't require a specific one. Units may be derived from `result.meta.units` if present, or left empty or null; missing units alone shouldn't fail a fix. A fix that removes the flag branch entirely (always using `StyledSimpleTableChart`) avoids the bug but drops the feature. Treat it as weaker, not the intended fix.

items.defectStatement: transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling (lines 47-65) only rewrites a column whose lowercased, stripped text is exactly "count()". Equivalent forms such as "count( )", "COUNT()" with internal whitespace, or an aliased "count() as total" pass through unchanged. For fully allowlisted error queries these columns then return raw, unweighted counts instead of upsampled ones.
obligations: Any y-axis column that is semantically a bare count() aggregate (case-insensitive, tolerant of whitespace inside or around the parentheses) must be rewritten to use upsampled_count().

If the original column carried an alias (e.g. "count() as total"), the transformed column must keep that alias rather than forcing "as count". The plain count() case must still produce a result keyed as "count", i.e. "upsampled_count() as count".

Columns that are not a bare count() must be returned unchanged and in their original order. This includes count(field), count_unique(...), and other aggregates or functions whose names merely contain "count".
The function signature and return type (list[str]) must be preserved.
items.notes: Several approaches are valid: a regex such as ^\s*count\s*\(\s*\)\s*(as\s+\w+)?\s*$ (case-insensitive), or parsing the column with an existing Sentry function/alias parser. The grader should not require use of the search/equation parser. Two traps to check for. First, a naive substring or startswith match that also transforms count(x), count_unique, count_if and similar must be rejected. Second, dropping the user's alias or changing the output key for the plain case breaks callers. Whether aliased y-axis entries actually reach this function is not shown in the code, so the alias part of the finding is plausible but somewhat speculative. Equations containing count() (e.g. "equation|count() * 2") are out of scope unless the fix explicitly handles them; leaving them unchanged is acceptable.

items.defectStatement: In `OrderedQueueWorker.run`, the `finally` block calls `offset_tracker.complete_offset` even when `result_processor` raised. The failed message's offset therefore becomes committable and is committed by `_commit_loop`, so Kafka never redelivers it: the message is dropped after only a log line. This contradicts the strategy's documented guarantee that it 'Only commits offsets after successful processing'.
obligations: When `result_processor` raises an `Exception`, the work item's offset must not be marked complete, so it stays outstanding and blocks commits past it for that partition. Retrying before giving up is also acceptable.
On successful processing, `complete_offset(work_item.partition, work_item.offset)` must still be called.
The queue-depth `metrics.gauge` must still be emitted on both success and failure, and the exception must still be logged via `logger.exception`.
Existing `queue.ShutDown` handling (break out of the loop) must be preserved.

items.defectStatement: In getSubGroups (lines 176-180), the diff dropped the hoisted `canViewGlobal = auth.groups().canView()` check. The filter now calls `auth.groups().canView(g)` for every subgroup, and that call is a full per-group permission evaluation. Because `getSubGroupsStream` is fetched unpaginated (-1, -1) and filtered before pagination, a global viewer now pays one evaluation per subgroup the stream consumes, where before it paid a single global check.
obligations: When the caller has global group view permission, getSubGroups must not run a per-subgroup canView(g) evaluation. The global check is computed once per request, not once per element.
For callers without global view, subgroups must still be filtered per group with canView(g), so only viewable subgroups are returned.

Keep the existing semantics: requireView(group) up front, the search/exact handling, filtering before paginatedStream(first, max), and the populateSubGroupCount/toRepresentation mapping with the briefRepresentation flag.
items.notes: Valid fixes include restoring `boolean canViewGlobal = auth.groups().canView();` with `.filter(g -> canViewGlobal || auth.groups().canView(g))`, or branching so the filter is skipped entirely when canViewGlobal is true. Trap: calling `auth.groups().canView()` inside the lambda still evaluates once per element and is not a fix. The diff does not show whether the V2 canView(g) already short-circuits internally on global view, so the cost may be smaller than claimed. Even so, restoring the hoisted check is correct and changes no behavior. The 'one evaluation into N' framing is accurate for the filtered elements, though paginatedStream may stop consuming early.

items.defectStatement: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no per-client resource exists, the fallback resource from getResourceTypeResource(...) for the Clients type may be null. It is then passed straight to policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and later dereferenced by resource.getScopes(). A missing "all-clients" type resource therefore causes an NPE or failure instead of denying permission.
obligations: When the fallback Clients resource-type resource is null, the method must return false (deny) without calling findByResource or dereferencing the resource.
Preserve existing behavior when the fallback resource exists: return false if it has no associated policies, otherwise proceed to evaluation with that resource.
Do not change the path where the per-client resource is found by findByName.
items.notes: The null check can be placed before findByResource or merged into the same condition (e.g. resource == null || ...isEmpty()). Either is valid as long as a null resource short-circuits to false. Whether getResourceTypeResource can actually return null is not visible in the shown code. It is plausible, given that the sibling overload guards the equivalent lookup, so the defensive check is reasonable. A fix that only guards findByResource but still reaches resource.getScopes() with null is incorrect.

items.defectStatement: The diff added an organization/BROKER_PUBLIC clause to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() (line 254). Every consumer of this SPI predicate now also rejects org-linked IDPs whose BROKER_PUBLIC is not "true". That includes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate(), which filters the user's already-linked federated identities, so those IDPs silently vanish from the linked-provider list.
obligations: When the fix is limited to the cited lines, getLoginPredicate() must return to its prior behavior: nonNull AND the ENABLED/LINK_ONLY/HIDE_ON_LOGIN filters, with no organizationId/BROKER_PUBLIC condition.

Org-linked IDPs with BROKER_PUBLIC unset or false that are enabled, not link-only and not hidden must pass getLoginPredicate() again, so existing callers such as IdentityProviderBean's federated-identity filtering are unaffected.
If the org/BROKER_PUBLIC check is still needed (e.g. for login-cache invalidation), it must live in a separate predicate or method and not in the shared getLoginPredicate().
items.notes: Adding a new method such as getLoginCachePredicate() that combines getLoginPredicate() with the org clause is valid, and so is simply removing the clause from the cited lines. Changing IdentityProviderBean instead is outside the cited lines and cannot be done here. Do not accept a fix that only reorders or rewrites the clause while keeping it inside getLoginPredicate(). The finding is not fully verifiable from the shown code, because the IdentityProviderBean usage and the cache-invalidation consumer are not shown. The shared-predicate regression itself is evident from the diff.

items.defectStatement: The removal listener (lines 77-96) checks only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1), but `management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. With both features on, role/client/group removal calls the V2 `setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)`, which reportedly throws `UnsupportedOperationException` and breaks the deletion. With only V2 on, the listener does nothing, so no permission cleanup runs for deleted entities.
obligations: When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled (with or without V1), deleting a role, client or group must not throw from this listener; the V1-only `setPermissionsEnabled` path must not be reached through a V2 management object.
When only V1 is enabled, behaviour is unchanged: the V1 implementation disables permissions for the removed role (client-role or realm-role realm resolution preserved), client and group.
When neither feature is enabled, the listener must remain a no-op for these events.
Cleanup with V2 enabled is either skipped or done through a V2-supported path; it must not call V1-only APIs on V2 objects.
items.notes: The `UnsupportedOperationException` in `ClientPermissionsV2` is not visible in the shown code; it is taken from the finding. Any of these fixes is acceptable: gate on V1-enabled and V2-disabled; instantiate `MgmtPermissions` directly for the V1 branch while skipping or separately handling V2; or add a V2 cleanup branch that uses V2-supported operations. Requiring full V2 resource or policy cleanup is likely overstated, since V2 may clean up elsewhere and that is not visible here. The essential fix is avoiding the V1 call on V2 objects and keeping V1 cleanup intact.

items.defectStatement: ClientPermissionsV2.canView() (lines 85-88) returns canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(VIEW) and never checks the fine-grained MANAGE scope on the all-clients resource. An admin granted only MANAGE on all-clients gets canManage()==true but canView()==false, so any view-all/list-clients check built on canView() is denied. This is inconsistent with canView(ClientScopeModel), which accepts VIEW || MANAGE, and with the role-based model, where manage-clients implies view.
obligations: canView() must return true when the caller holds the MANAGE scope on the all-clients resource, even without the VIEW scope.
canView() must still return true when canViewClientDefault() is true or when the VIEW scope on all-clients is granted.
canView() must still return false when the caller has neither VIEW nor MANAGE on all-clients and no default view/manage admin role.
The change must not introduce recursion: canView(ClientModel) calls canView(), and canManage() must not end up calling canView().
items.notes: Valid fixes include adding `|| hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` or delegating to `canManage()`; both are acceptable. canManage() is super.canManage() || hasPermission(MANAGE), so delegating also covers the manage-clients role, which canViewClientDefault() likely already covers. The role-based manage-clients path is probably not broken; the gap is the fine-grained MANAGE scope. Per-client canView(ClientModel) already partly honors MANAGE through canConfigure -> canManage(client), so the defect lies in the global canView() and whatever list checks depend on it.

items.defectStatement: When the common prefix and common suffix of `value` and `sanitized` overlap, `start + end` exceeds the length of the shorter string. For example, value="aaa" and sanitized="aa" give start=2 and end=2. The substring calls on line 111 then get an end index smaller than the begin index (`value.substring(2,1)`, `sanitized.substring(2,0)`) and throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, which aborts the verifier instead of recording an "Illegal HTML" message.
obligations: No StringIndexOutOfBoundsException for any pair of distinct strings `value`/`sanitized`, including overlapping prefix/suffix runs (e.g. "aaa" vs "aa", "ab" vs "abab") and either string being empty or a prefix/suffix of the other.
An "Illegal HTML in key ... for file ...: '<x>' vs. '<y>'" message is still added for every mismatching key, with the same message format.
When prefix and suffix do not overlap, the shown differing segments are identical to the current output (same start/end computation).
The two snippets stay consistent: each shown segment is a valid substring of its own string, and concatenating prefix + segment + suffix reconstructs that string.
items.notes: The finding is valid. Several fixes are acceptable: bound the suffix loop by `min(value.length(), sanitized.length()) - start`, or clamp the substring indices as the finding suggests. Bounding the suffix loop gives the more meaningful diff. The finding's clamp avoids the exception but may show an empty or less accurate segment; it is still acceptable. A fix that guards only the `value` substring and not the `sanitized` substring is incomplete, because both throw. Wrapping the code in try/catch and dropping the message is not acceptable.

items.defectStatement: GrafanaRuleListItem passes only the Prometheus rule (`promRule={rule}`) to RuleActionsButtons, with no ruler rule. Per the finding, AlertRuleMenu renders MenuItemPauseRule only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` is true, so Grafana rules in the new list lose the Pause/Resume action even when the user is allowed to pause.
obligations: Grafana alerting and recording rules shown by GrafanaRuleListItem must render a working Pause/Resume menu action when the user has the pause permission.
The pause action must still target the correct rule (uid / group identifier) and reflect its current paused state (`rule.isPaused`).
Other existing actions (edit, view, more menu, compact mode) and the groupIdentifier wiring must keep working.
The line must still type-check against RuleActionsButtons' props, whether it passes extra data (e.g. a ruler rule obtained from a hook) or relies on updated downstream components.
items.notes: The cited line alone may not be enough. A fix confined to line 47 is only valid if it supplies ruler rule data, for example from a hook defined elsewhere, or if RuleActionsButtons/AlertRuleMenu are adapted to accept the prom rule. Accept either approach: fetching ruler data on demand, or making the pause component and menu work from the GrafanaPromRuleDTO (uid, isPaused). AlertRuleMenu's code is not shown, so the claim that it requires the ruler rule comes from the finding and cannot be verified here; treat it as plausible. Do not accept a fix that shows the pause item without being able to perform the pause.

items.defectStatement: At line 139 the asynchronous legacy update is given the caller's original objInfo, not the object that unified storage already committed (`res`). Legacy storage re-applies objInfo.UpdatedObject (e.g. a patch) against its own possibly stale copy, so the legacy result can differ from unified storage or fail, even though the unified update succeeded. The previous code wrapped the committed object in an updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: obj}; the diff removed that wrapping.
obligations: The legacy Update call must receive a rest.UpdatedObjectInfo whose UpdatedObject returns the object committed by unified storage (`res`), not one recomputed from objInfo against legacy's old object.
Preconditions and other upstream objInfo behavior must still be delegated to the original objInfo, e.g. via an updateWrapper with upstream: objInfo and updated: res.
The legacy update must stay in the background goroutine with the timeout context and legacy duration metric recording, and the function must still return res, async, err from unified storage.
items.notes: Building an equivalent wrapper inline is fine if it serves the committed object and delegates Preconditions to objInfo. A fix that only reorders code but still passes the raw objInfo is wrong. Other issues in this file are out of scope for this line: the wrong metric call on the storage-error path at line 129, and recordStorageDuration being used for legacy in DeleteCollection.

items.defectStatement: In DualWriterMode3.Delete (lines 99-105), any error from Storage.Delete, including NotFound, returns immediately and skips the legacy delete. The previous code treated IsNotFound as tolerable and still deleted from Legacy. As a result, objects that exist only in legacy storage are never removed and remain as orphaned copies.
obligations: When Storage.Delete returns a NotFound error, Legacy.Delete must still be invoked for the same name, deleteValidation and options, either synchronously or in the existing async goroutine.
Storage errors other than NotFound must still log, record the storage failure metric, and return early without touching Legacy.
The successful Storage path must remain unchanged: return res/async/err from storage and perform the legacy delete with its timeout and metrics.
In the NotFound case the caller must still get a coherent result. The old behavior returned the storage NotFound error, and preserving that is acceptable.
items.notes: The diff removed the apierrors import, so a fix using apierrors.IsNotFound needs that import restored outside the cited lines; don't penalize this. Accept either approach to legacy deletion in the NotFound case: synchronous like the old code, or reusing the async goroutine. A fix that returns the legacy delete's result instead of the storage NotFound error is debatable; the old code returned the storage error. These existing bugs are outside the cited lines and are not required: line 106 passes name instead of options.Kind; line 97 uses d.Log instead of log; Create and Update record legacy instead of storage metrics on failure.

items.defectStatement: TotalDocs ranges over b.cache (line 146) without holding b.cacheMu, while BuildIndex writes b.cache under cacheMu (lines 137-139). A concurrent map read and write can trigger Go's fatal "concurrent map read and map write" error or a race-detector failure, for example during metrics collection.
obligations: TotalDocs must read b.cache only while holding b.cacheMu: a read lock if cacheMu is a sync.RWMutex, or Lock if it is a sync.Mutex.
The lock must be released on every path, so no deadlock or leaked lock is possible.
TotalDocs must keep its semantics: it sums DocCount across all cached indexes, skips indexes whose DocCount returns an error, and returns an int64.
BuildIndex must still store idx in b.cache under the lock and return idx, nil.
items.notes: The finding says the old code serialized this access, which is overstated. Before the PR, only BuildIndex took the lock and TotalDocs never did, so the reader was unsynchronized even then. The race predates the PR, though the defect itself is real. The declared type of cacheMu is not shown. RLock is only valid for a sync.RWMutex; Lock is acceptable either way. Two approaches are both valid: holding the lock for the whole loop, or copying the indexes under the lock and calling DocCount after unlocking. Re-adding a lock around the whole of BuildIndex without locking TotalDocs does not fix the race.

items.defectStatement: After the diff made `rule` optional, `RuleActionsButtons.V2` can render from only a Grafana `promRule`. `handleSilence` still sets `showSilenceDrawer`, but `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` renders only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true (line 104). So in the list view, where `rule` is undefined, choosing Silence from the menu flips state and nothing appears.
obligations: When `rule` is undefined and `promRule` is a Grafana alerting rule, clicking Silence must render a silence drawer populated with that rule's data (at minimum its uid/identifier), not nothing.
Existing behavior must be preserved: when a Grafana ruler alerting rule is provided, the drawer still renders with that rule exactly as before.
The drawer must stay gated on `showSilenceDrawer`, and `onClose` must still reset it to false.
No drawer should render for non-Grafana or recording rules, and the code must not crash or pass undefined where the drawer needs rule data.
items.notes: `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` currently takes `rulerRule`, so a complete fix may need it to accept a rule UID or a prom rule instead, or the component may fetch the ruler rule by uid. All of these are valid. The fix may also touch the drawer component outside the cited lines, but the cited JSX must change its condition and props. Trap: only widening the condition while still passing `rule={undefined}` is not a fix. Whether `AlertRuleMenu` even shows Silence for prom-only rules is not visible here; grade the drawer rendering.

items.defectStatement: At line 97 the result of `parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` is stored directly as `credential.key`. The helper returns a Zod safeParse-style wrapper (`{ success, data }`), not the credential object, so the DB row gets the wrapper instead of `{ access_token, refresh_token, expiry_date, ... }`. The next `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (line 75) then fails, breaking the credential after its first token refresh.
obligations: The value written to `credential.key` must be the flat parsed Google credential object (top-level access_token, refresh_token, expiry_date, scope, token_type), not a `{ success, data }` wrapper.
The persisted key must contain the refreshed access_token and expiry_date set on lines 95-96.
The DB update must still target `credential.id`, and the rest of the refresh flow, including `myGoogleAuth.setCredentials` and the catch/invalid_grant handling, must be unchanged.
items.notes: Valid fixes include taking `.data` from the helper result, destructuring `{ data }`, or reverting to `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)`. Using `.data` without checking `success` can persist `undefined` if the parse fails; a fix that guards on `success` or throws is acceptable but not required. The helper's body is not shown, so the claim about its return shape comes from the finding and is consistent with its name. Changes outside lines 97-100 are not needed.

items.defectStatement: tagDeviceUI writes the device's cache key (line 87) before CreateOrUpdateDevice runs. When the store fails, for example with ErrDeviceLimitReached, TagDevice returns the error at lines 144-148 but leaves the cache entry in place. The next request from that device hits the cache, tagDeviceUI returns nil, and the over-limit device is authenticated anonymously for the rest of the 29-minute cache TTL.
obligations: When tagDeviceUI returns an error, the cache entry for this device must not remain. A later request from the same device must go through CreateOrUpdateDevice again and be rejected again while still over the limit.
Any removed or skipped cache entry must use exactly the same key that tagDeviceUI computes for this device; deleting a differently formatted key does nothing.
TagDevice must still return the error from tagDeviceUI so Authenticate rejects the request, and must keep the debug log.
On success, the device is still cached and nil is returned, so repeat requests within the TTL still skip the DB write.
items.notes: The key derivation in tagDeviceUI is above line 84 and not shown, so a fix in the cited lines must recompute the same key, or call a shared helper, before calling localCache.Delete. Setting the cache only after a successful write inside tagDeviceUI is equally valid but lies outside the cited lines; accept it if paired correctly. Clearing the cache on any store error, not just ErrDeviceLimitReached, is acceptable and arguably better.

items.defectStatement: Both cleanup registrations in testCacheIDPForLogin (line 381 inside the creation loop, and line 425 after creating idp-alias-20) target an IDP with the literal alias "alias", which never exists. Because of this, none of the 21 created providers (idp-alias-0..19 and idp-alias-20) are removed after the test. They leak into later tests, and each cleanup call fails against a nonexistent resource.
obligations: The loop cleanup must remove the IDP created in that iteration ("idp-alias-" + i). The alias must be captured per iteration, either via an eagerly evaluated method-reference receiver or an effectively final local; a lambda reading the loop variable `i` won't compile.
The cleanup after creating the hide-on-login provider must remove "idp-alias-20".
All other code in the cited range must stay behaviorally unchanged: IDP creation attributes, org linking, and the cache assertions with their expected counts (5/5/10).

items.defectStatement: Line 13 interpolates the raw `url` into a single-quoted href attribute and into the link text with no HTML escaping. The result is appended to contents that are stored with the raw_html cook method, so a URL containing `'`, `<`, or `>` can break out of the attribute or tag. For example, `http://host/x'onmouseover='alert(1)` injects an event handler, giving stored XSS.
obligations: Both uses of `url` on line 13 (href value and link text) must be HTML-escaped, or the anchor built through an API that escapes, so quotes and angle brackets cannot end the attribute or open new markup.
Normal http/https URLs must still produce a working link with the same visible text inside the imported_from footer, wrapped in `<hr>` and `<small>` as before.
The original `url` must remain unchanged for the later embed lookup, the SHA1, the stored embed_url and absolutize_urls. Only the interpolated HTML may use the escaped form.
`url` must not be mutated in place (for example with gsub!).
items.notes: Any of these is acceptable: ERB::Util.html_escape / CGI.escapeHTML / Rack::Utils.escape_html, or building the anchor with Nokogiri. Escaping that misses single quotes is not acceptable while the attribute stays single-quoted; ERB::Util.html_escape does cover `'`. Switching to double quotes without escaping is insufficient. Restricting the scheme is not required: line 11 already allows only http/https, so the risk is attribute or markup injection, not javascript: URLs. Whether the caller validates only the host cannot be confirmed from this file, and it does not matter, because import_remote and import accept arbitrary url strings.

items.defectStatement: The password check (line 121) runs only when `credentials.totpCode` is empty, but the backup-code branch (lines 131-157) runs whenever `backupCode` is present and never looks at `totpCode`. A request with any dummy `totpCode` plus a valid `backupCode` therefore skips both password and TOTP verification, so anyone with the email and one leaked backup code can log in without the password.
obligations: A login with a non-empty `totpCode` and a valid `backupCode` must not succeed unless the account password has been verified. Either verify the password in the backup-code path or reject requests that carry both fields.
If the fix verifies the password in the backup-code path, a missing `user.password` or a wrong password must be rejected with `IncorrectEmailPassword`. It must not fall through to success.

Existing legitimate behavior must be preserved: correct password, valid backup code and no `totpCode` still logs in and consumes that code (it is nulled and re-encrypted). Wrong or missing backup codes still raise `IncorrectBackupCode` / `MissingBackupCodes`. The TOTP branch is unchanged.

A backup code must not be consumed (persisted as null) when the request is going to be rejected for the bypass condition, so the password or conflict check must happen before the `prisma.user.update`.
items.notes: The finding is accurate. Two valid fixes exist: (a) inside the backup branch, explicitly call `verifyPassword(credentials.password, user.password)` and throw on failure or when no password exists; (b) throw when both `totpCode` and `backupCode` are supplied, which makes line 121 run for backup logins. Fix (b) also closes the related skip of the third-party-IdP checks at lines 113/117, which a dummy `totpCode` would otherwise bypass. Fix (a) does not close that skip, though that gap is a secondary concern. Do not accept a fix that only reorders branches or strips `totpCode` without forcing a password check. The fix is limited to lines 131-157, so changes to line 121 are out of scope, but checks placed at the top of the backup branch are fine.
